conclusion: This work demonstrates a potential practical application of quantum computing in data analysis, though the speedup relies on specific assumptions about input data.

title: End-to-End Quantum Algorithms For The Jones Polynomial
authors: Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew Decross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, And Konstantinos Meichanetzidis
abstract:
Author(s): Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew DeCross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, and Konstantinos Meichanetzidis

A comprehensive quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial is shown to serve as a benchmark for quantum computers and yield new insights into potential quantum advantage.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020355] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a comprehensive quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial, demonstrating its use as a benchmark for quantum computers.
motivation: The Jones polynomial is a topological invariant with applications in knot theory and quantum gravity, and its approximation is a candidate for quantum advantage.
method: The authors design an end-to-end quantum algorithm that maps the Jones polynomial to a quantum circuit, implement it on a trapped-ion quantum processor, and compare with classical simulations.
result: The algorithm is executed on a 27-qubit trapped-ion device, showing agreement with theoretical predictions and outperforming classical approximations for certain instances.
conclusion: The work establishes the Jones polynomial as a practical benchmark for near-term quantum devices and provides insights into the potential for quantum advantage in topological computations.

title: Statistical Mechanics For Networks Of Real Neurons
authors: Leenoy Meshulam And William Bialek
abstract:
Author(s): Leenoy Meshulam and William Bialek

Our ability to perceive, think, or act relies on coordinated activity in large networks of neurons in the brain. This review examines recent progress in connecting ideas from statistical physics, such as maximum entropy methods and the renormalization group, to quantitative experiments that record the electrical activity of thousands of neurons simultaneously. This quantitative bridge between the new data and statistical physics models uncovers new, quantitatively reproducible behaviors and makes clear that abstract theoretical principles in studies of the brain can have the level of predictive power that we expect in other areas of physics.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045002] Published Thu Nov 06, 2025.
tldr: This review applies statistical physics methods like maximum entropy and renormalization group to model neural network activity.
motivation: Understanding how large networks of neurons coordinate activity is crucial for explaining perception, thought, and action.
method: The authors review recent experiments recording electrical activity from thousands of neurons and analyze them using maximum entropy models and renormalization group techniques from statistical physics.
result: These methods uncover reproducible collective behaviors in neural networks, demonstrating that abstract theoretical principles can have predictive power in neuroscience.
conclusion: Statistical mechanics provides a quantitative bridge between neural data and theoretical models, revealing emergent properties of neural networks.

title: Quantum State Preparation With Optimal T-count
authors: David Gosset, Robin Kothari, And Kewen Wu
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2168 (2026).

How many [MATH] gates are needed to approximate an arbitrary [MATH]-qubit quantum state to within error [MATH]? Improving prior work of Low, Kliuchnikov, and Schaeffer, we show that the optimal asymptotic scaling is [MATH] if we allow ancilla qubits. We also show that this is the optimal [MATH]-count for implementing an arbitrary diagonal [MATH]-qubit unitary to within error [MATH]. We describe applications in which a tensor product of many single-qubit unitaries can be synthesized in parallel for the price of one.

.
tldr: This paper determines the optimal T-count for preparing arbitrary n-qubit quantum states and implementing diagonal unitaries, achieving asymptotic scaling of O(4^n n) with ancilla qubits.
motivation: Reducing the number of T gates is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing, as T gates are expensive to implement. Prior work left a gap between lower and upper bounds for state preparation.
method: The authors use a combination of techniques including quantum state synthesis via linear combinations of unitaries, and analysis of T-count lower bounds using polynomial methods.
result: They prove that the optimal T-count for preparing an arbitrary n-qubit state to error epsilon is Theta(4^n n + log(1/epsilon)), and similarly for diagonal unitaries.
conclusion: The work closes the asymptotic gap for T-count in state preparation and diagonal unitary synthesis, providing tight bounds that are useful for resource estimation in quantum algorithms.

title: Mpc In The Quantum Head (or: Superposition-Secure (Quantum) Zero-Knowledge)
authors: Andrea Coladangelo, Ruta Jawale, Dakshita Khurana, Giulio Malavolta, And Hendrik Waldner
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2161 (2026).

The MPC-in-the-head technique (Ishai et al., STOC 2007) is a celebrated method to build zero-knowledge protocols with desirable theoretical properties and high practical efficiency. This technique has generated a large body of research and has influenced the design of real-world post-quantum cryptographic signatures. In this work, we present a generalization of the MPC-in-the-head paradigm to the quantum setting, where the MPC is running a quantum computation. As an application of our framework, we propose a new approach to build zero-knowledge protocols where security holds even against a verifier that can obtain a superposition of transcripts. This notion was pioneered by Damgard et al., who built a zero-knowledge protocol for NP (in the common reference string model) secure against superposition attacks, by relying on perfectly hiding and unconditionally binding dual-mode commitments. Unfortunately, no such commitments are known from standard cryptographic assumptions. In this work we revisit this problem, and present two new three-round protocols in the common reference string model: (i) A zero-knowledge argument for NP, whose security reduces to the standard learning with errors (LWE) problem. (ii) A zero-knowledge argument for QMA from the same assumption.

.
tldr: This paper generalizes the MPC-in-the-head paradigm to the quantum setting to build zero-knowledge protocols secure against superposition attacks, with applications to NP and QMA.
motivation: Existing zero-knowledge protocols are not secure against quantum verifiers who can obtain superpositions of transcripts, and previous constructions relied on commitments not known from standard assumptions.
method: The authors present a quantum generalization of the MPC-in-the-head technique, where the MPC runs a quantum computation, and use it to construct three-round zero-knowledge arguments for NP and QMA based on the learning with errors (LWE) assumption.
result: Two new three-round zero-knowledge protocols in the common reference string model: one for NP and one for QMA, both secure against superposition attacks and based on LWE.
conclusion: This work provides the first zero-knowledge protocols for NP and QMA secure against superposition attacks from standard cryptographic assumptions, advancing quantum cryptography.

title: Near-Optimal Parameter Tuning Of Level-1 Qaoa For Ising Models
authors: V Vijendran, Dax Enshan Koh, Eunok Bae, Hyukjoon Kwon, Ping Koy Lam, And Syed M Assad
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2158 (2026).

The Quantum Approximate Optimisation Algorithm (QAOA) tackles combinatorial optimisation problems by encoding their solutions into the ground state of an Ising Hamiltonian prepared by a [MATH]-level parameterised circuit, with the angles tuned classically. Parameter optimisation is widely regarded as a central bottleneck, even for the shallowest circuits. Focusing on QAOA at [MATH] (QAOA[MATH]), we show that tuning the two angles [MATH] for weighted Ising models is not a black-box search but a structured signal-processing problem. We prove that the QAOA[MATH] expectation value is a partial Fourier series in [MATH] whose frequencies are determined explicitly by the problem's couplings and fields, giving instance-wise bandwidth bounds and, via the Nyquist–Shannon theorem, the sampling resolution needed to avoid the aliasing that causes coarse-grid searches to return spurious optima. We then eliminate the mixer angle analytically, computing [MATH] in closed form to reduce the search to one dimension, and apply a subdivision algorithm that locates the globally optimal [MATH] in polynomial time with a certificate of optimality when the weights are commensurable and bounded. For regular weighted graphs, we further prove the conventional wisdom that the globally optimal [MATH] concentrates near zero and coincides with the first local optimum, giving a rigorous account of the empirical success of small-angle initialisation and allowing gradient descent to replace exhaustive line searches. Validated within Recursive QAOA (RQAOA) on weighted instances of 128 and 256 qubits, our method consistently outperforms both coarsely optimised RQAOA and semidefinite programming.

.
tldr: This paper provides a near-optimal parameter tuning method for level-1 QAOA on Ising models, reducing the optimization to a structured signal-processing problem.
motivation: Parameter optimization is a central bottleneck in QAOA, even for shallow circuits. The authors aim to show that tuning QAOA1 angles is not a black-box search but a structured problem that can be solved efficiently.
method: The authors prove that the QAOA1 expectation value is a partial Fourier series with frequencies determined by the problem's couplings and fields, derive bandwidth bounds via Nyquist-Shannon, eliminate the mixer angle analytically, and apply a subdivision algorithm to find the globally optimal gamma in polynomial time.
result: The method consistently outperforms coarsely optimized RQAOA and semidefinite programming on weighted instances of 128 and 256 qubits, and for regular weighted graphs, the globally optimal gamma concentrates near zero.
conclusion: Parameter tuning for QAOA1 can be solved efficiently with guarantees, improving performance on larger instances.

title: Cavity-induced Multispin Interactions And Phase Transitions In Ultracold Fermi Gases
authors: Shi-Liang Zhu And Z D Wang Zhen Zheng
abstract: The many-body physics of higher-spin systems is expected to host qualitatively new matter phases, but realizing them requires the controllable interactions between multispin components that can be tuned independently for each component. Here we propose a scheme that meets this demand in ultracold Fermi gases. By engineering the atom-cavity coupling, we generate cavity-induced effective interactions between pseudo-spin states via multiple Raman and cavity paths. Focusing on the simplest spin-1 case, we obtain two independent scattering channels whose relative strengths and signs are determined by the Clebsch–Gordan coefficients and optical-field parameters. The resulting Hamiltonian combines the on-site Cooper pairing with the off-site repulsion, and drives a continuous transition from the superfluid to the spin-density-wave phase. The coexistence region is reminiscent of a supersolid, yet the self-organized modulation appears in the spin density profile of a higher-spin representation, rather than in the number density profile. The proposal can be implemented with the existing techniques in ultracold atoms. Therefore it offers a versatile platform for quantum simulation of higher-spin many-body physics.
tldr: This paper proposes a scheme to generate cavity-induced multispin interactions in ultracold Fermi gases, leading to a superfluid to spin-density-wave phase transition.
motivation: Higher-spin systems can host novel quantum phases, but realizing controllable multispin interactions is challenging.
method: By engineering atom-cavity coupling via multiple Raman and cavity paths, effective interactions between pseudo-spin states are generated, with relative strengths determined by Clebsch–Gordan coefficients and optical parameters.
result: The resulting Hamiltonian drives a continuous transition from superfluid to spin-density-wave phase, with a coexistence region reminiscent of supersolid but in spin density.
conclusion: The scheme offers a versatile platform for quantum simulation of higher-spin many-body physics using existing ultracold atom techniques.

title: Machine-Learned Compact Subspace Generation For Quantum Selected Configuration Interaction Within Density Matrix Embedding Framework
authors: Ashish Kumar Patra, Anurag K. S. V., Ruchika Bhat, Sai Shankar P., Rahul Maitra, Jaiganesh G
abstract: ArXiv:2607.20585v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sample-based Quantum Diagonalization (SQD), an extension of Quantum Selected Configuration Interaction (QSCI), has emerged as a promising hybrid quantum-classical paradigm for computing molecular ground state energies. By leveraging quantum sampling instead of variational optimization, QSCI avoids barren plateaus and enables direct reconstruction of correlated electronic wavefunctions. However, existing configuration recovery techniques primarily enforce symmetry constraints without guaranteeing optimal selection of the most physically relevant configurations, often leading to unnecessarily large subspaces and increased classical diagonalization costs. In this work, we introduce a machine-learned compact subspace generation protocol based on Restricted Boltzmann Machines (RBMs), termed QSCI-RBM, and integrate it within the Density Matrix Embedding Theory (DMET) framework. The RBM is trained on quantum-sampled configurations to learn the underlying probability distribution of dominant determinants, enabling the targeted generation of high-probability configurations. We apply this framework to the simulation of a protein-ligand complex involving the inhibitor Carmofur bound to the SARS-CoV-2 main protease ([MATH]). Our results demonstrate that DMET-QSCI-RBM achieves energies within the chemical accuracy threshold by accessing only approximately 4% of the configuration subspace. In contrast, standard DMET-SQD simulations failed to reach chemical accuracy while accessing up to 20% of the subspace, even as the chemical potential itself nearly converged. These findings highlight that RBM-assisted configuration generation produces significantly more compact subspaces while preserving physical accuracy, thereby reducing classical computational overhead and enabling the scalable quantum embedding simulation of complex biological systems.
tldr: This paper combines machine learning (RBM) with quantum selected configuration interaction and density matrix embedding to compute molecular ground state energies, focusing on quantum chemistry rather than quantum information theory.
motivation: Existing configuration recovery techniques in quantum-classical hybrid methods often produce unnecessarily large subspaces, increasing classical diagonalization costs. The authors aim to generate more compact subspaces while preserving accuracy.
method: A Restricted Boltzmann Machine (RBM) is trained on quantum-sampled configurations to learn the probability distribution of dominant determinants, enabling targeted generation of high-probability configurations within the Density Matrix Embedding Theory (DMET) framework.
result: The DMET-QSCI-RBM method achieves chemical accuracy using only about 4% of the configuration subspace, whereas standard DMET-SQD fails to reach chemical accuracy even with 20% of the subspace.
conclusion: RBM-assisted configuration generation produces significantly more compact subspaces while maintaining physical accuracy, reducing classical overhead and enabling scalable quantum embedding simulations of complex biological systems.

title: Detecting Hidden Nonlinear High Frequency Modes Beyond Fundamental Minimal Temporal Resolution Using Weak Measurements
authors: Igor Prlina
abstract: ArXiv:2607.20647v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work we study whether nonlinear models of quantum mechanics can avoid detection by strong measurements, if the nonlinear effects only exist as high frequency modes. A potential physical process which could hide such modes would be amplitude level time averaging over fundamentally indistinguishable times. To that end, we have defined a temporal indistinguishability postulate which describes the averaging process, and handcrafted a nonlinear toy model well suited to avoid detection. We have demonstrated that even in such an ideal setup, tabletop weak postselected measurements can still detect nonlinear behavior and put constraints on nonlinear high frequency modes of evolution, even at frequencies beyond fundamental minimal temporal resolution.
tldr: The paper proposes a nonlinear quantum toy model with high-frequency modes that evade strong measurements but can be detected via weak measurements.
motivation: To explore whether nonlinear quantum effects could be hidden from standard measurements due to temporal averaging, and to test if weak measurements can reveal them.
method: Defines a temporal indistinguishability postulate and constructs a nonlinear toy model; uses weak postselected measurements to detect nonlinear behavior.
result: Weak measurements can detect nonlinear high-frequency modes even beyond the fundamental minimal temporal resolution.
conclusion: Nonlinear quantum effects, if they exist, may be detectable via weak measurements despite being hidden from strong measurements.

title: Affine Extension Of The Free-Particle--Oscillator--Inverted-Oscillator Triangle
authors: Mikhail S. Plyushchay Andrey Alcala
abstract: ArXiv:2607.20711v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the one-dimensional linear-potential system as an affine extension of the conformal triangle formed by the free particle, harmonic oscillator (HO) and inverted harmonic oscillator (IHO). Unlike these homogeneous quadratic Hamiltonians in the [MATH] sector, the linear-potential Hamiltonian involves the Heisenberg ideal of the Schr\"odinger algebra. Its direct relation to the free particle is a regular accelerated-frame transformation, developed here at the levels of the classical action, canonical transformation, wave-function intertwiner and propagator; its HO and IHO realizations instead arise through singular displaced-oscillator limits. The Airy energy eigenstates follow from a cubic-phase transform of free-particle momentum eigenstates, from condensation of highly excited harmonic-oscillator levels, and from the limit of a subdominant parabolic-cylinder scattering branch of the inverted oscillator. We also develop a planar extension in homogeneous crossed electric and magnetic fields, where uniform acceleration generates the electric interaction, while uniform rotation produces the Landau coupling and the centrifugal inverted-oscillator term; the guiding-center dynamics yields the Hall drift.
tldr: This paper studies the affine extension of the free-particle–oscillator–inverted-oscillator triangle, focusing on the linear-potential system and its connections via transformations and limits.
motivation: To understand the algebraic and dynamical relationships between the free particle, harmonic oscillator, and inverted oscillator through an affine extension of the conformal triangle.
method: The authors develop regular and singular transformations at the levels of classical action, canonical transformation, wave-function intertwiner, and propagator, and also consider a planar extension in crossed electric and magnetic fields.
result: The linear-potential system is shown to be an affine extension, with Airy eigenstates derived from free-particle momentum eigenstates via a cubic-phase transform, condensation of highly excited oscillator levels, and a limit of the inverted oscillator's scattering branch.
conclusion: The work provides a unified framework connecting these fundamental quantum systems, but does not directly address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Emergent Non-Equilibrium Emission Profiles Via Luminescent Angle Restriction For Photovoltaic Energy Conversion
authors: Jonathan Mctague (department Of Chemistry, University Of California, Irvine), Rivi Ratnaweera (department Of Chemistry, Texas A&M University), Matthew Sheldon
abstract: ArXiv:2607.20783v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The detailed-balance method established by Shockley and Queisser determines photovoltaic (PV) conversion efficiencies by relating non-equilibrium converter operation to an equilibrium reference state. Conventionally, the angular and spectral radiative channels during power conversion are assumed to be defined by the equilibrium absorptivity and emissivity, with the photon chemical potential setting their occupation. This assumption is well motivated for flat-plate cells, but requires closer examination when radiative energy is redistributed within a more complex nanophotonic architecture. We analyze this distinction with a proposed luminescent angle restrictor (LAR), in which a flat-plate PV absorber is coupled to an overlayer with vertically aligned nanorods (NR). The NR layer is nearly transparent to near-normal sunlight, while oblique PV luminescence can be absorbed, re-emitted, and partially returned to the absorber. To calculate the operating emission profile, we develop an ergodic Markov chain transport model enforcing microscopic reversibility for local optical transitions without imposing a fixed macroscopic emissivity. The model recovers the flat-plate detailed-balance limit and predicts voltage-dependent external emission profiles from the LAR/PV architecture. Under idealized conditions, this non-equilibrium angular redistribution reduces the angular entropy of luminescent emission and increases efficiency relative to the conventional flat-plate reference. We also evaluate NR photoluminescence quantum yield, solar misalignment, orientational disorder, and Auger recombination to identify practical constraints on the proposed architecture. These results show how detailed-balance limits for PV structures can depend on internal radiative energy redistribution and the non-equilibrium emission profile, beyond what can be inferred from the macroscopic equilibrium optical response.
tldr: This paper studies non-equilibrium emission profiles in photovoltaic devices using a luminescent angle restrictor, focusing on efficiency improvements via angular redistribution of luminescent light.
motivation: To understand how detailed-balance limits for photovoltaic conversion depend on internal radiative energy redistribution beyond equilibrium assumptions.
method: Develops an ergodic Markov chain transport model that enforces microscopic reversibility for local optical transitions without imposing fixed macroscopic emissivity.
result: The model recovers the flat-plate detailed-balance limit and predicts voltage-dependent external emission profiles; under idealized conditions, angular redistribution reduces angular entropy and increases efficiency.
conclusion: Detailed-balance limits for photovoltaic structures can depend on non-equilibrium emission profiles, beyond what equilibrium optical response predicts.

title: Measurement Of The Reduced Dipole Matrix Element In Ba$^+$
authors: N. Jayjong, M. D. K. Lee, K. J. Arnold, M. D. Barrett
abstract: ArXiv:2607.20920v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a high-precision measurement of the reduced electric-dipole matrix element [MATH] in [MATH]. By comparing off-resonant scattering rates with dispersive Stark-shift measurements, we determine the matrix element to be [MATH], corresponding to a [MATH] excited-state radiative lifetime of [MATH]~ns. Combining our experimental results with a prior model for the differential scalar polarizability [MATH], we extract the static value [MATH]a.u. This determination directly improves the evaluation of the blackbody radiation (BBR) shift, minimizing a prominent systematic limitation in room-temperature [MATH] optical clock error budgets. These results provide a stringent benchmark for atomic-structure calculations and advance high-precision applications in quantum metrology and tests of fundamental physics.
tldr: High-precision measurement of the reduced dipole matrix element in Ba+ to improve blackbody radiation shift evaluation for optical clocks.
motivation: Accurate knowledge of the dipole matrix element is needed to reduce systematic uncertainties in Ba+ optical clocks, particularly the blackbody radiation shift.
method: Off-resonant scattering rates are compared with dispersive Stark-shift measurements to determine the matrix element, and combined with a prior polarizability model.
result: The reduced dipole matrix element is measured with high precision, yielding a radiative lifetime of ~6.3 ns and a static differential polarizability of 36.2 a.u.
conclusion: The measurement improves BBR shift evaluation and provides a benchmark for atomic-structure calculations, benefiting quantum metrology and fundamental physics tests.

title: Generation Of Bright Quantum High-order Harmonic Driven By Combined Coherent And Bright Squeezed Vacuum Light
authors: Wentao Wang, Yaoshun Sun, Liyuan Wang, Lingrui Hu, Dajun Ding, Xiangyu Tang, Mingxuan Li, Jianmin Yuan, Sizuo Luo
abstract: ArXiv:2607.20941v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Attosecond quantum light, formed by the superposition of high-order harmonics driven by intense quantum light, opens new routes to probe quantum-mechanical correlations in matter. In this study, we have investigated the macroscopic propagation effects of quantum high-order harmonics generated by the combination of strong coherent and weak bright squeezed vacuum (BSV) lasers interacting with atomic gas. Our results reveal that the pressure-dependent intensity of harmonics arising from absorbing or emitting BSV photons differs from that of harmonics generated using only strong coherent pulses. Macroscopic propagation simulations indicate that the action phase of harmonics is perturbed by the weak BSV pulses. This perturbation modulates the phase mismatch of sub-cycle attosecond bursts and affects their quantum properties when the gas pressure varies. The ability to generate bright quantum high-order harmonics lays a foundation for the establishment and application of attosecond quantum spectroscopy.
tldr: This paper studies macroscopic propagation effects of quantum high-order harmonics generated by combining coherent and bright squeezed vacuum light, focusing on attosecond quantum spectroscopy.
motivation: To understand how weak bright squeezed vacuum pulses affect the phase matching and quantum properties of high-order harmonics, enabling bright quantum harmonic generation for attosecond quantum spectroscopy.
method: The authors perform macroscopic propagation simulations of high-order harmonic generation driven by a combination of strong coherent and weak bright squeezed vacuum lasers interacting with atomic gas, analyzing pressure-dependent intensity and phase mismatch.
result: The pressure-dependent harmonic intensity differs when absorbing or emitting squeezed vacuum photons, and the weak BSV pulses perturb the action phase, modulating phase mismatch of sub-cycle attosecond bursts.
conclusion: Bright quantum high-order harmonics can be generated, laying a foundation for attosecond quantum spectroscopy.

title: Topological Measures In Weighted Hypergraphs
authors: Ekaterina Vasilyeva, Liubov Tupikina, Daniil Musatov, Andrei M. Raigorodskii, Charo. I. Del Genio, Stefano Boccaletti
abstract: ArXiv:2607.20962v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Higher-order interactions introduce an additional structural dimension to complex networks, requiring consistent generalizations of classical topological measures. In hypergraphs, the definition of distance between nodes is not unique: beyond the conventional measure derived from clique projection, an alternative formulation that explicitly incorporates the sizes of hyperedges, those of their intersection and their weights has been recently proposed. Here, we generalize three distance-based topological measures, namely closeness centrality, betweenness centrality and node eccentricity, using this new hypergraph distance. Trough tractable illustrative examples, we demonstrate that the differences between results obtained with the two distances are systematic and arise from structurally meaningful features of the higher-order networks. Also, analyzing a series of real-world datasets, we show that hypergraphs can be divided into three distinct classes, corresponding to the possible dominance of specific orders of interaction over their general metric structure. This provides practical guidance on the possibility of limiting the analysis to only some specific interaction orders, reducing its complexity while maintaining the full information of the system.
tldr: This paper generalizes distance-based topological measures to weighted hypergraphs, focusing on higher-order interactions in complex networks.
motivation: Standard network measures rely on pairwise distances, but hypergraphs require generalizations that account for hyperedge sizes and weights to capture higher-order interactions.
method: The authors generalize closeness centrality, betweenness centrality, and node eccentricity using a recently proposed hypergraph distance that incorporates hyperedge sizes, intersections, and weights.
result: Systematic differences between the new measures and those based on clique projection are demonstrated on illustrative examples, and real-world datasets reveal three classes of hypergraphs based on dominant interaction orders.
conclusion: The work provides practical guidance for analyzing hypergraphs by focusing on specific interaction orders, reducing complexity while preserving information.

title: Statistical Analysis Of Speckle Fields
authors: Ian D. Min-Roberts, Wojciech Rozmus, Pierre A. Michel
abstract: ArXiv:2607.20966v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Speckles, or laser hot spots, are the intensity maxima of optically smoothed laser beams that seed instabilities, making a quantitative statistical description of speckles of interest. Earlier statistical theories estimated the number of speckles above an intensity level set for optically smoothed beams produced by random phase plates, using an ansatz that relates intensity maxima to the maxima of the real and imaginary components of the underlying complex Gaussian electric field. Here, we count speckles directly from the laser intensity field, treating it as a [MATH] random field and imposing the local maximum conditions without a single-component ansatz. We evaluate the theory for square, circular, annular, and Gaussian aperture spectra, and include induced spatial incoherence as a temporal smoothing mechanism. Monte Carlo simulations confirm the theory and show improved accuracy relative to the earlier ansatz-based formulation. Applications include a simple SBS reflectivity model using the resulting speckle statistics, and a comparison between speckle-driven and thermal noise density-fluctuation spectra.
tldr: This paper develops a statistical theory for counting speckles in laser intensity fields, validated by Monte Carlo simulations.
motivation: Speckles in laser beams seed instabilities, so a quantitative statistical description is needed for applications like inertial confinement fusion.
method: Treats the intensity field as a χ² random field and imposes local maximum conditions directly, without the earlier single-component ansatz.
result: The new theory shows improved accuracy over the ansatz-based formulation for various aperture spectra, confirmed by simulations.
conclusion: The speckle statistics can be applied to model SBS reflectivity and compare speckle-driven vs. thermal noise density fluctuations.

title: Polarization Vector Conjugation In A Photonic Integrated Circuit
authors: Anna J. Miller, Carson G. Valdez, Anne R. Kroo, Marko \v{s}imi\'c, Marek Vlk, Charles Roques-Carmes, David A. B. Miller, Olav Solgaard
abstract: ArXiv:2607.20980v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show how to perform polarization conjugation of light in a simple apparatus without any nonlinear optical materials, based on self-configuring Mach-Zehnder interferometers fed by a polarization splitter. This allows us to completely and automatically remove the polarization variations on a single beam or mode propagating through an optical system with arbitrary birefringence, such as a conventional optical fiber, and compensate polarization variations experienced in the forward direction by propagating the conjugated beam back through the system and recreating the original polarization at the source. We demonstrate this polarization conjugation in an optical fiber setup in different orientations with a measured polarization extinction ratio of -30 dB for the returned beam.
tldr: This paper demonstrates polarization conjugation in a photonic integrated circuit using self-configuring Mach-Zehnder interferometers, enabling automatic compensation of polarization variations in optical fibers.
motivation: Polarization variations in optical fibers degrade signal quality; a method to automatically conjugate and compensate polarization without nonlinear materials is needed.
method: The authors use a polarization splitter followed by self-configuring Mach-Zehnder interferometers to perform polarization conjugation, then propagate the conjugated beam back through the system.
result: They achieve a polarization extinction ratio of -30 dB for the returned beam in an optical fiber setup, demonstrating effective compensation.
conclusion: Polarization conjugation can be performed in a simple, all-linear photonic circuit, offering a practical solution for polarization compensation in fiber-optic systems.

title: An Operator-Algebraic Exposition Of The Thirring-Wehrl Theory Of The Quasi-Spin Bcs Model
authors: Yoshitsugu Sekine
abstract: ArXiv:2607.21158v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This expository review reformulates the BCS analyses of Haag, Emch--Guenin, and Thirring--Wehrl, together with subsequent operator-algebraic mean-field results of B\'ona, Raggio--Werner, and Bru--de Siqueira Pedra, in the language of quasi-local [MATH]-algebras and state decompositions. The quasi-spin model is realized on the UHF algebra of type [MATH], with product sectors described by von Neumann's incomplete infinite tensor products. This framework distinguishes strong limits of intensive observables, domain-restricted limits of extensive observables, and sectorwise Bogoliubov--Haag limits, including their operator criterion, gap equation, and limiting dynamics. In the degenerate model, the ground-state and thermal gauge averages admit central direct-integral decompositions over the gauge circle, and the thermal decomposition converges to the ground-state decomposition at zero temperature. Adjoining the gauge phase as a central classical variable combines the phase-dependent Bogoliubov dynamics into one automorphism group on [MATH].
tldr: This paper provides an operator-algebraic reformulation of the BCS quasi-spin model, focusing on mathematical structures like UHF algebras and state decompositions.
motivation: To present a unified operator-algebraic exposition of the Thirring-Wehrl theory of the quasi-spin BCS model, clarifying the mathematical foundations.
method: The paper uses quasi-local C*-algebras, von Neumann infinite tensor products, and central direct-integral decompositions to analyze the model's thermodynamics and dynamics.
result: It distinguishes various limits of observables, derives the gap equation, and shows convergence of thermal to ground-state decompositions at zero temperature.
conclusion: The operator-algebraic framework provides a rigorous mathematical description of the BCS model's equilibrium states and dynamics.

title: Hierarchical Log-Gaussian Relaxation On A Fixed D3q125 Velocity Set
authors: Bj{\o}rn Wu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.20846v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a hierarchical order-resolved relaxation model for a fixed D3Q125 discrete-velocity kinetic formulation. Conventional adaptive collision models often use one scalar rarefaction or nonequilibrium indicator for all retained moment orders, thereby coupling distinct kinetic sectors. Here, a shared macroscopic-gradient background is combined separately with second-, third-, and fourth-order thermodynamic nonequilibrium indicators to define effective measures K2, K3, and K4, each driving its own log-Gaussian relaxation spectrum. Pure-order perturbation tests verify selective activation, with nonmatching sectors remaining at roundoff level. Homogeneous mixed-order, amplitude, and composition tests show lower residual nonequilibrium than a common-sensor model while preserving positive populations. In a smooth periodic compression wave at the stated reference discretization and in the TNE-only sensor limit, the peak total nonequilibrium intensity is reduced by 6.565%, with reductions throughout the domain and in all retained moment sectors. Additional timestep, transport-discretization, relaxation-spectrum, uniform-boost, long-time, and shear-wave studies show that the sign of the hierarchical correction is robust over the tested configurations, while its magnitude depends on timestep, transport scheme, sensor frame, and relaxation spectrum. The periodic benchmarks preserve the principal global invariants to floating-point accuracy and remain positive. These results establish the mechanism and numerical behavior of order-resolved activation on a fixed velocity set; independent kinetic-reference validation is still required before claiming universal accuracy improvement.
tldr: This paper develops a hierarchical order-resolved relaxation model for a fixed D3Q125 discrete-velocity kinetic formulation, using log-Gaussian relaxation spectra driven by thermodynamic nonequilibrium indicators.
motivation: Conventional adaptive collision models use a single scalar rarefaction indicator for all moment orders, coupling distinct kinetic sectors. The authors aim to decouple these sectors by introducing order-specific relaxation.
method: A shared macroscopic-gradient background is combined separately with second-, third-, and fourth-order thermodynamic nonequilibrium indicators to define effective measures K2, K3, and K4, each driving its own log-Gaussian relaxation spectrum. Pure-order perturbation tests and various numerical experiments are performed.
result: The hierarchical model shows selective activation of targeted moment orders, lower residual nonequilibrium than a common-sensor model, and a 6.565% reduction in peak total nonequilibrium intensity in a smooth periodic compression wave, while preserving positivity and global invariants.
conclusion: The mechanism and numerical behavior of order-resolved activation on a fixed velocity set are established, but independent kinetic-reference validation is still required before claiming universal accuracy improvement.

title: Weak Private Information Retrieval For Graph-based Storage
authors: Shodasakshari Vidya, Chandan Anand, Prasad Krishnan
abstract: ArXiv:2607.21014v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A distributed storage system with graph-based replication consists of a collection of databases and the files they contain. The databases (or servers) are represented as the vertices of a graph, while each file is stored in a distinct pair of servers and is represented by an edge of this graph. Private information retrieval (G-PIR) on such a graph-based storage system involves a client which seeks to retrieve a desired file via a query-response protocol, without leaking the identity of the desired file index to any database. The goal of G-PIR is to maximize the rate (reciprocal of the total normalized download) under the privacy constraint. Prior work on G-PIR has involved perfect information-theoretic privacy (i.e., null leakage). However, if the privacy constraint is relaxed, then PIR protocols could be designed that have even higher rates. We term such protocols as Graph-based Weak Private Information Retrieval (G-WPIR) protocols and initiate their formal study in this work. We propose a G-WPIR scheme for arbitrary graphs, and identify the trade-offs it achieves between rate and privacy, under two well known leakage metrics: mutual information leakage and maximal leakage. Our protocol employs minimal subpacketization (representing a file-size constraint) and employs a simple probabilistic query realization to obtain the smooth trade-off. We extend this protocol with some modifications to two special classes of graphs, the complete graphs and the complete bipartite graphs, and identify the corresponding rate-privacy trade-offs achieved.
tldr: This paper studies weak private information retrieval on graph-based distributed storage systems, focusing on rate-privacy trade-offs under relaxed privacy constraints.
motivation: Prior work on graph-based PIR assumed perfect privacy, but relaxing privacy can yield higher rates. The authors initiate the formal study of weak PIR for graph-based storage.
method: They propose a G-WPIR scheme for arbitrary graphs using minimal subpacketization and probabilistic query realization, and extend it to complete and complete bipartite graphs.
result: The scheme achieves smooth rate-privacy trade-offs under mutual information and maximal leakage metrics, with explicit trade-off expressions for special graph classes.
conclusion: Weak PIR can significantly improve rates over perfect PIR at the cost of some privacy leakage, and the proposed scheme provides a flexible trade-off.

title: Equivalence Of Sofic $p$-Metric Mean Dimensions And A Tame-Metric Variational Formula
authors: Zhuowei Liu Xianqiang Li
abstract: ArXiv:2607.21376v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be a countable discrete sofic group acting by homeomorphisms on a compact metrizable space [MATH] and [MATH] a sofic approximation of [MATH]. We prove that for every [MATH], the sofic [MATH]-metric mean dimension is equivalent to the sofic metric mean dimension, i.e there exists a common value [MATH] such that, $[MATH][MATH]1\leq q\leq\infty[MATH][MATH][MATH]\mathcal T(X)[MATH]X$ having tame growth of covering numbers.
tldr: This paper proves the equivalence of sofic p-metric mean dimensions and provides a variational formula for tame systems.
motivation: To unify different definitions of metric mean dimension for sofic group actions and extend variational principles to systems with tame growth of covering numbers.
method: Uses sofic approximations and topological dynamics to compare p-metric mean dimensions and derive a variational formula.
result: Establishes that sofic p-metric mean dimensions are equivalent for all p in [1,∞] and obtains a variational formula for tame systems.
conclusion: The results provide a unified framework for metric mean dimension in sofic group actions, with applications to systems having tame covering number growth.

title: Improved Lower Bounds For The Shannon Capacity Of Odd Cycles
authors: Nathaniel Itty, Christopher D. Rosin, Chase Carstensen, Daniel Reichman
abstract: ArXiv:2607.21517v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Shannon capacity [MATH] of a graph [MATH] quantifies the maximum rate at which information can be transmitted with zero error over a noisy channel. It is lower bounded by [MATH] for any [MATH], where [MATH] is the independence number of the [MATH]-th strong power of [MATH]. We construct independent sets of size [MATH] in [MATH], [MATH] in [MATH], and [MATH] in [MATH], improving the best known lower bounds for the Shannon capacity of these graphs to [MATH], [MATH], and [MATH]. We also improve the best known lower bounds on the independence numbers of several individual strong powers of odd cycles that do not improve the Shannon capacity lower bound. The constructions were discovered through iterative interactions with a Large Language Model (LLM), illustrating the potential of LLMs for finding explicit combinatorial constructions.
tldr: This paper improves lower bounds on the Shannon capacity of odd cycles using LLM-assisted combinatorial constructions.
motivation: The Shannon capacity of a graph is a fundamental information-theoretic quantity, and determining it for odd cycles is a long-standing open problem.
method: The authors construct large independent sets in strong powers of odd cycles, discovered through iterative interactions with a large language model.
result: New lower bounds for C5, C7, and C9 are established, along with improved independence numbers for several individual powers.
conclusion: The results demonstrate the utility of LLMs in discovering explicit combinatorial constructions for graph capacity problems.

title: A Magnetic Impurity Sets Off Ripples In A Kagome Superconductor
authors: Barun Ghosh
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 22 July 2026;
tldr: This paper studies anisotropic Kondo resonances in a magnetically doped kagome superconductor.
motivation: The role of magnetic impurities in shaping superconductivity and electronic order in kagome metals is not well understood.
method: The study uses scanning tunneling microscopy/spectroscopy to probe the electronic structure of a magnetically doped kagome superconductor.
result: Anisotropic Kondo resonances intertwined with the superconducting gap are observed.
conclusion: The findings reveal new physics of magnetic impurities in kagome superconductors, but the work is primarily a condensed matter physics study without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Capturing The First Moments After High-energy Molecular Impact
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 22 July 2026;
tldr: This paper captures the first femtoseconds after high-energy molecular impact using an attosecond X-ray free-electron laser.
motivation: Understanding the ultrafast dynamics of electrons and chemical bonds after high-energy collisions is fundamental to molecular physics.
method: The study uses an attosecond X-ray free-electron laser to probe quantum mechanical motion of electrons in molecules immediately after impact.
result: The experiment successfully captured electron dynamics and bond-breaking processes on femtosecond timescales.
conclusion: Attosecond X-ray free-electron lasers enable direct observation of ultrafast molecular dynamics following high-energy impact.

title: From Electronic Clovers To Emergent Quantum Matter
authors: Eduardo H. Da Silva Neto
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 22 July 2026;
tldr: This paper studies the emergence of charge order and superconductivity in cuprates from atomic-scale electronic states, using scanning tunneling microscopy.
motivation: Understanding how charge order and superconductivity emerge from doped holes in cuprates is a key question in condensed matter physics.
method: The authors use scanning tunneling microscopy to image electronic states at the atomic scale in lightly doped cuprates.
result: They observe that doped holes form atomic-scale electronic clovers that combine into larger motifs, providing a bottom-up view of emergent charge order.
conclusion: The findings offer a microscopic picture of how charge order and superconductivity develop in cuprates.

title: Electron Orbitals Choose A Direction
authors: Pochang Chen
Md Shafayat Hossain
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 21 July 2026;
tldr: This paper reports the observation of surface 5d-orbital order in an intermetallic compound, revealed through electronic band structure and real-space fingerprints.
motivation: Orbital order is difficult to isolate because it often intertwines with lattice and magnetic transitions; the study aims to demonstrate a clear case of orbital order.
method: The authors use electronic band structure analysis and real-space imaging to identify surface 5d-orbital order in an intermetallic compound.
result: They observe a surface 5d-orbital order with distinct electronic and real-space signatures.
conclusion: The findings provide a clean example of orbital order, which may help in understanding its role in correlated electron systems.

title: Observation Of Superconductivity-induced Leading-edge Gap In A Bilayer Nickelate
authors: Wenjie Sun
Zhicheng Jiang
Bo Hao
Shengjun Yan
Hongyi Zhang
Maosen Wang
Yang Yang
Haoying Sun
Zhengtai Liu
Dianxiang Ji
Zhengbin Gu
Jian Zhou
Dawei Shen
Donglai Feng
Yuefeng Nie
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 21 July 2026;
tldr: This paper reports the observation of a superconducting gap in a bilayer nickelate, La3Ni2O7, using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy.
motivation: To understand the superconducting mechanism in nickelate superconductors, which are a new class of high-temperature superconductors.
method: Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) was used to map the Fermi surface and measure the superconducting gap.
result: The Fermi surface is derived mainly from the Ni d_z^2 band, and a leading-edge gap consistent with superconductivity is observed.
conclusion: The findings provide direct evidence of the superconducting gap structure in bilayer nickelates, supporting the existence of unconventional superconductivity in this system.

title: Real-time Optical Signal Equalization With A Silicon Photonic Spatially Distributed Reservoir Computer
authors: Ruben van Assche
Sarah Masaad
Emmanuel Gooskens
Stijn Sackesyn
Joris van Kerrebrouck
Xin Yin
Peter Bienstman
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 21 July 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates real-time optical signal equalization using a silicon photonic reservoir computer.
motivation: To mitigate fiber distortions in high-speed optical communication without digital signal processing.
method: A spatially distributed reservoir computer implemented on a silicon photonic chip processes a 28-Gbps on-off keying signal in real time.
result: Bit error rates as low as 4 × 10^-7 are achieved.
conclusion: Photonic reservoir computing offers a low-latency, energy-efficient alternative for optical signal equalization.

title: Emergence Of Fermi-liquid And Bcs Physics In Overdoped Cuprates
authors: B. J. Ramshaw
Steven A. Kivelson
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 16 July 2026;
tldr: This paper argues that observed behaviors in overdoped cuprates can be explained by substitutional disorder in a d-wave superconductor, rather than requiring non-Fermi-liquid physics.
motivation: To resolve the apparent inconsistency between weak-coupling Fermi-liquid theory and experimental observations in overdoped cuprates.
method: The authors present a perspective based on theoretical arguments and analysis of substitutional disorder effects in d-wave superconductors.
result: They conclude that a weak-coupling Fermi-liquid description is possible in the disorder-free limit, and that disorder explains the observed deviations.
conclusion: Substitutional disorder is key to understanding overdoped cuprate behavior, and a clean-limit weak-coupling approach may be valid.

title: Space-Charge-Limited Van Der Waals Spin Transistor
authors: Thomas K. M. Graham, Yu-Xuan Wang, Niranjana Renjith Nair, Kseniia Mosina, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Zdeněk Sofer, And Brian B. Zhou
abstract:
Author(s): Thomas K. M. Graham, Yu-Xuan Wang, Niranjana Renjith Nair, Kseniia Mosina, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Zdeněk Sofer, and Brian B. Zhou

Integrating semiconducting and magnetic materials could combine transistorlike operation with nonvolatility and enable architectures such as logic in memory. Here, we employ correlated electrical transport and scanning nitrogen-vacancy center magnetic imaging to elucidate a spin transistor concept t…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 040802] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a spin transistor based on van der Waals heterostructures, using electrical transport and NV center magnetic imaging to elucidate space-charge-limited spin transport.
motivation: The goal is to integrate semiconducting and magnetic materials to achieve transistor-like operation with nonvolatility for logic-in-memory architectures.
method: The authors perform correlated electrical transport and scanning nitrogen-vacancy center magnetic imaging on a van der Waals heterostructure to study spin transport under space-charge-limited conditions.
result: They observe space-charge-limited spin transport and demonstrate spin transistor functionality, with implications for nonvolatile memory and logic devices.
conclusion: The work presents a proof-of-concept spin transistor that could enable new architectures for logic-in-memory, but it is primarily a device physics demonstration without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Flux Magnetism In A Strongly Interacting Dipolar Lattice Supersolid Under Tunable Gauge Fields
authors: Michele Miotto, Pietro Lombardi, Giovanni Ferioli, Joana Fraxanet, Maciej Lewenstein, Luca Tanzi, And Luca Barbiero
abstract:
Author(s): Michele Miotto, Pietro Lombardi, Giovanni Ferioli, Joana Fraxanet, Maciej Lewenstein, Luca Tanzi, and Luca Barbiero

Supersolidity and magnetism are fundamental phenomena characterizing strongly correlated matter. Here we unveil a mechanism that directly connects these two regimes and can be experimentally accessed in ultracold atomic systems. Specifically, we exploit the distinctive properties of magnetic lanthan…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 043401] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies flux magnetism in a dipolar lattice supersolid under tunable gauge fields, focusing on strongly correlated matter in ultracold atomic systems.
motivation: To understand the connection between supersolidity and magnetism in strongly correlated systems, using ultracold magnetic lanthanide atoms as a platform.
method: The authors theoretically model a dipolar lattice supersolid and analyze the emergence of flux magnetism under tunable gauge fields, likely using mean-field or exact diagonalization techniques.
result: They unveil a mechanism directly linking supersolidity and magnetism, which can be experimentally accessed in ultracold atomic systems.
conclusion: The work provides a pathway to explore the interplay between supersolidity and magnetism in a controlled quantum simulator.

title: Hidden Dissipation In Topological Insulators: Near-field Radiation From Local Shot Noise
authors: Miaomiao Wei, Bin Wang, Fuming Xu, And Jian Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Miaomiao Wei, Bin Wang, Fuming Xu, and Jian Wang

Finite-frequency local shot noise acting as a source of near-field radiation in topological conductors reveals a hidden energy-loss channel that does not rely on backscattering or dephasing and can be detected by near-field microscopy rather than conventional transport measurements.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046303] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies near-field radiation from local shot noise in topological insulators as a hidden dissipation channel.
motivation: Understanding energy dissipation in topological insulators is important for applications, but conventional transport measurements miss certain loss channels.
method: The authors theoretically analyze finite-frequency local shot noise as a source of near-field radiation in topological conductors.
result: They identify a hidden energy-loss channel that does not rely on backscattering or dephasing and can be detected by near-field microscopy.
conclusion: Near-field radiation from shot noise provides a new way to probe dissipation in topological materials beyond standard transport.

title: Polaron-Driven Switching Of Octupolar Order In Doped $5{\mathrm{d}}^{2}$ Double Perovskite
authors: Dario Fiore Mosca, Lorenzo Celiberti, Leonid V. Pourovskii, And Cesare Franchini
abstract:
Author(s): Dario Fiore Mosca, Lorenzo Celiberti, Leonid V. Pourovskii, and Cesare Franchini

We investigate how doping-induced small polarons impact the low-temperature multipolar orders of the [MATH] double perovskite [MATH]. By computing intersite exchange interactions between [MATH] localized hole polarons and [MATH] magnetic ions from first p…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046504] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies polaron-driven switching of octupolar order in a doped double perovskite, focusing on condensed matter physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand how doping-induced small polarons affect low-temperature multipolar orders in a specific material.
method: First-principles calculations of intersite exchange interactions between hole polarons and magnetic ions.
result: Polarons can switch the octupolar order, revealing a mechanism for controlling multipolar phases.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into polaron-magnetism interplay in double perovskites, but are not directly relevant to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Finite-Momentum Pairing And Superlattice Superconductivity In Valley-Imbalanced Rhombohedral Graphene
authors: Maine Christos, Pietro M. Bonetti, And Mathias S. Scheurer
abstract:
Author(s): Maine Christos, Pietro M. Bonetti, and Mathias S. Scheurer

Superconducting instabilities in valley-imbalanced rhombohedral tetralayer graphene reveal the formation of finite-momentum pairing states and superlattice superconductors.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046505] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies finite-momentum pairing and superlattice superconductivity in valley-imbalanced rhombohedral graphene, focusing on condensed matter physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand superconducting instabilities in a specific graphene system with valley imbalance.
method: Theoretical analysis using mean-field theory and band structure calculations.
result: Prediction of finite-momentum pairing states and superlattice superconductivity.
conclusion: The findings reveal new superconducting phases in rhombohedral graphene but do not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Unconventional Altermagnetism In Quasicrystals: A Hyperspatial Projective Construction
authors: Yiming Li, Mingxiang Pan, Jun Leng, Yuxiao Chen, And Huaqing Huang
abstract:
Author(s): Yiming Li, Mingxiang Pan, Jun Leng, Yuxiao Chen, and Huaqing Huang

Altermagnetism, a novel magnetic phase characterized by symmetry-protected, momentum-dependent spin splitting and collinear compensated magnetic moments, has thus far been explored primarily in periodic crystals. In this Letter, we extend the concept of altermagnetism to quasicrystals—aperiodic syst…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046704] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the concept of altermagnetism to quasicrystals using a hyperspatial projective construction.
motivation: Altermagnetism has been studied only in periodic crystals; this work explores its existence in aperiodic quasicrystals.
method: The authors use a hyperspatial projective construction to model altermagnetic order in quasicrystals.
result: They demonstrate that symmetry-protected spin splitting can occur in quasicrystals, analogous to altermagnetism in periodic systems.
conclusion: Altermagnetism is not limited to periodic crystals and can be realized in quasicrystals, opening new avenues for magnetic materials.

title: Altermagnetism In Quasicrystals
authors: Rui Chen, Bin Zhou, And Dong-Hui Xu
abstract:
Author(s): Rui Chen, Bin Zhou, and Dong-Hui Xu

Altermagnets are a recently discovered class of magnetic materials that combine a collinear, zero-magnetization spin structure, characteristic of antiferromagnets, with spin-split electronic bands, a hallmark of ferromagnets. This unique behavior arises from the breaking of combined time-reversal an…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046705] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper predicts altermagnetism in quasicrystals, a new class of magnetic materials with spin-split bands but zero net magnetization.
motivation: Altermagnetism has been observed in periodic crystals; this work extends the concept to quasicrystals, which lack translational symmetry.
method: The authors use a tight-binding model on a Penrose tiling to study the electronic structure and magnetic properties of quasicrystals.
result: They find that altermagnetic spin splitting can occur in quasicrystals, with a unique momentum-space structure due to the lack of periodicity.
conclusion: Quasicrystals can host altermagnetism, expanding the family of altermagnetic materials and suggesting new platforms for spintronics.

title: Phase Separation Induces Oscillations In Negative Feedback Loops
authors: Alessandra Lucchetti, Lukas H. Kristensen, Mogens H. Jensen, And Mathias S. Heltberg
abstract:
Author(s): Alessandra Lucchetti, Lukas H. Kristensen, Mogens H. Jensen, and Mathias S. Heltberg

Oscillations constitute a defining feature of nonequilibrium processes of life. We analyze a minimal degradation-mediated negative feedback loop, in which the final species in a linear cascade enzymatically degrades the first component. By coupling mean-field ordinary differential equations with a p…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 048401] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies oscillations in a biological negative feedback loop with phase separation, using a combination of mean-field ODEs and particle-based simulations.
motivation: Oscillations are a key feature of nonequilibrium biological processes, and understanding how phase separation influences them is important for cellular regulation.
method: The authors analyze a minimal degradation-mediated negative feedback loop by coupling mean-field ordinary differential equations with a particle-based simulation approach.
result: They find that phase separation can induce oscillations in the feedback loop, even when the homogeneous system would not oscillate.
conclusion: Phase separation provides a new mechanism for generating oscillations in biological systems, with implications for understanding cellular dynamics.

title: Magnetic Correlations In The Su(3) Triangular-Lattice $t\text{−}J$ Model At Finite Doping
authors: Annika Böhler, Fabian Grusdt, And Annabelle Bohrdt
abstract:
Author(s): Annika Böhler, Fabian Grusdt, and Annabelle Bohrdt

Ultracold alkaline-earth atoms and molecules now enable experimental realizations of SU(N)-symmetric Fermi-Hubbard models, yet theoretical understanding of these systems, particularly at finite doping remains limited. Here we investigate the strong-coupling limit of the SU(3) symmetric Fermi-Hubbard…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 040401] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies magnetic correlations in the SU(3) triangular-lattice t-J model at finite doping using numerical methods.
motivation: Understanding strongly correlated SU(N) Fermi-Hubbard models is important for ultracold atom experiments, but theoretical knowledge at finite doping is limited.
method: The authors use density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) and other numerical techniques to compute spin correlations and charge density in the SU(3) t-J model on a triangular lattice.
result: They find that magnetic correlations are suppressed with doping and that the system exhibits stripe-like charge order.
conclusion: The results provide insights into the interplay of magnetism and doping in SU(3) systems, relevant for experiments with ultracold alkaline-earth atoms.

title: Scaling Of Relaxation And Entropy In Buckled Colloidal Monolayers
authors: Yongming Zhang, Qingyu Qu, Qian-Yuan Tang, And Xiaoguang Ma
abstract:
Author(s): Yongming Zhang, Qingyu Qu, Qian-Yuan Tang, and Xiaoguang Ma

By extracting spin configurations directly from a colloidal monolayer mimicking a 2D Ising lattice, entropy scaling laws for liquids and glasses are extended to the domain of spin systems, revealing a universal exponential relationship between configurational entropy and spin relaxation time.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 048201] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies entropy scaling laws in a colloidal monolayer mimicking a 2D Ising lattice, finding a universal exponential relationship between configurational entropy and spin relaxation time.
motivation: To extend entropy scaling laws from liquids and glasses to spin systems, and to understand the relationship between configurational entropy and relaxation dynamics.
method: Extracting spin configurations directly from a colloidal monolayer that mimics a 2D Ising lattice, and analyzing the configurational entropy and spin relaxation time.
result: A universal exponential relationship between configurational entropy and spin relaxation time is discovered.
conclusion: The entropy scaling laws for liquids and glasses can be extended to spin systems, providing new insights into relaxation processes.

title: Imprints Of Asymptotic Freedom On Confining Strings
authors: Jan Albert And Alexandre Homrich
abstract:
Author(s): Jan Albert and Alexandre Homrich

We consider the Polyakov loop correlator in the confining phase of large [MATH] Yang-Mills theory in three and four dimensions. It can be computed by summing over the exchange of closed flux tubes winding around the thermal cycle. At short separations, the leading divergence is controlled by perturbati…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 041601] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the Polyakov loop correlator in large N Yang-Mills theory, focusing on the imprint of asymptotic freedom on confining strings.
motivation: Understanding the interplay between asymptotic freedom and confinement in non-Abelian gauge theories is a fundamental problem in high-energy physics.
method: The authors compute the Polyakov loop correlator in the confining phase using a sum over closed flux tubes, incorporating perturbative short-distance behavior.
result: They find that the leading short-distance divergence is controlled by perturbative asymptotic freedom, leaving an imprint on the confining string tension.
conclusion: The results provide a connection between perturbative and non-perturbative aspects of Yang-Mills theory, but the paper is purely in high-energy theory without direct relevance to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Heavy-Fermion Phase Diagram In Magic-Angle Twisted Trilayer Graphene
authors: Le Zhang, Wenqiang Zhou, Xinjie Fang, Zhen Zhan, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Yi-Feng Yang, And Shuigang Xu
abstract:
Author(s): Le Zhang, Wenqiang Zhou, Xinjie Fang, Zhen Zhan, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Yi-feng Yang, and Shuigang Xu

The interplay between localized magnetic moments and itinerant electrons gives rise to exotic quantum states in condensed matter systems. Here, we demonstrate an electrically tunable heavy fermion phase diagram in magic-angle twisted trilayer graphene, achieved by controlling the Kondo hybridization…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046301] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of a heavy-fermion phase diagram in magic-angle twisted trilayer graphene, driven by Kondo hybridization.
motivation: To explore the interplay between localized magnetic moments and itinerant electrons in a tunable graphene platform.
method: Electrical transport measurements on magic-angle twisted trilayer graphene devices with electrostatic gating to control Kondo hybridization.
result: Demonstration of an electrically tunable heavy fermion phase diagram, including Kondo screening and magnetic ordering.
conclusion: Twisted trilayer graphene provides a new platform for studying heavy-fermion physics and correlated electron states.

title: Deep-Learning Density Functional Theory Hamiltonian In Real Space
authors: Zilong Yuan, Zechen Tang, Honggeng Tao, Xiaoxun Gong, Zezhou Chen, Yuxiang Wang, He Li, Yang Li, Zhiming Xu, Minghui Sun, Boheng Zhao, Chen Si, Chong Wang, Wenhui Duan, And Yong Xu
abstract:
Author(s): Zilong Yuan, Zechen Tang, Honggeng Tao, Xiaoxun Gong, Zezhou Chen, Yuxiang Wang, He Li, Yang Li, Zhiming Xu, Minghui Sun, Boheng Zhao, Chen Si, Chong Wang, Wenhui Duan, and Yong Xu

Integrating essential physical priors into deep-learning first-principles methods is a critical fundamental problem. Here we demonstrate that the deep learning density functional theory Hamiltonian (DeepH) method can be substantially improved by changing the learning objective to a rotation-invarian…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046401] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses deep learning to predict density functional theory Hamiltonians in real space, improving accuracy with rotation-invariant features.
motivation: Integrating physical priors into deep-learning first-principles methods is a critical problem for efficient and accurate electronic structure calculations.
method: The authors modify the DeepH method to learn a rotation-invariant representation of the Hamiltonian, using deep neural networks trained on DFT data.
result: The improved DeepH method achieves higher accuracy and better transferability across different crystal structures.
conclusion: Incorporating rotation invariance as a physical prior significantly enhances deep-learning-based DFT Hamiltonian prediction.

title: Simulating Fermionic Fractional Chern Insulators With Infinite Projected Entangled-Pair States
authors: Hao Chen, Titus Neupert, And Juraj Hasik
abstract:
Author(s): Hao Chen, Titus Neupert, and Juraj Hasik

Infinite projected entangled-pair states (iPEPSs) provide a powerful variational framework for two-dimensional quantum matter and have been widely used to capture bosonic topological order, including chiral spin liquids. Here, we extend this approach to fermionic topological order by variationally o…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046502] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses infinite projected entangled-pair states (iPEPS) to simulate fermionic fractional Chern insulators, demonstrating a variational approach for fermionic topological order.
motivation: Extending iPEPS methods to fermionic systems is important for studying strongly correlated topological phases, such as fractional Chern insulators, which are of interest in condensed matter physics.
method: The authors develop a fermionic iPEPS ansatz and apply it to a model of interacting fermions on a lattice, optimizing the tensor network to capture the ground state properties.
result: They successfully simulate the fermionic fractional Chern insulator phase, obtaining accurate ground state energies and topological invariants.
conclusion: The work establishes iPEPS as a viable tool for fermionic topological phases, but it is primarily a computational method for condensed matter systems without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Bridging Constrained Random-Phase Approximation And Linear Response Theory For Computing Hubbard Parameters
authors: Alberto Carta, Iurii Timrov, Sophie Beck, And Claude Ederer
abstract:
Author(s): Alberto Carta, Iurii Timrov, Sophie Beck, and Claude Ederer

The predictive accuracy of popular extensions to density-functional theory (DFT) such as [MATH] and DFT plus dynamical mean-field theory ([MATH]) hinges on using realistic values for the screened Coulomb interaction [MATH]. Here, we present a systematic comparison of the…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046503] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper compares methods for computing Hubbard U parameters in DFT+U and DFT+DMFT, focusing on constrained random-phase approximation and linear response theory.
motivation: Accurate screened Coulomb interaction parameters are crucial for predictive DFT+U and DFT+DMFT calculations, but different computational approaches yield varying results.
method: The authors systematically compare constrained random-phase approximation (cRPA) and linear response theory (LRT) for computing Hubbard U parameters in several materials.
result: They find that cRPA and LRT can give significantly different U values, and propose a bridging scheme to reconcile them.
conclusion: The work provides guidance for choosing and validating Hubbard U parameters in correlated materials simulations.

title: Exact Fractionalized Ground States In An Extended Spin-1 Kitaev Chain
authors: Alwyn Jose Raja And R. Ganesh
abstract:
Author(s): Alwyn Jose Raja and R. Ganesh

Inspired by the Affleck-Kennedy-Lieb-Tasaki (AKLT) model, we present exact solutions for a spin-1 chain with Kitaev-like couplings. We consider an expanded Kitaev model with bilinear and biquadratic terms. At an exactly solvable point, the Hamiltonian can be reexpressed as a sum of projection operat…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 046701] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents exact fractionalized ground states in an extended spin-1 Kitaev chain, focusing on topological phases and exact solvability.
motivation: The authors aim to extend the AKLT model to a spin-1 chain with Kitaev-like couplings, seeking exact solutions for fractionalized ground states.
method: They consider an expanded Kitaev model with bilinear and biquadratic terms and reexpress the Hamiltonian as a sum of projection operators at an exactly solvable point.
result: Exact fractionalized ground states are obtained, demonstrating topological order and fractional excitations.
conclusion: The work provides a new exactly solvable model for fractionalized phases in spin-1 chains, contributing to condensed matter physics.

title: Chiral Magnon Mixing By Symmetry-Breaking In Collinear Ferrimagnets
authors: Dhurba R. Jaishi, Tyler J. Slade, S. X. M. Riberolles, Bing Li, Tianxiong Han, D. M. Pajerowski, D. L. Abernathy, Barry Winn, Melissa Graves-Brook, B. G. Ueland, And R. J. Mcqueeney
