A nonperturbative quantization framework for chiral solitons in spin chains demonstrates that they condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid, appearing as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase and becoming detectable via inelastic neutron scattering.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021056] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies quantum chiral solitons in spin chains and their condensation into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid, detectable via neutron scattering.
motivation: To develop a nonperturbative quantization framework for chiral solitons and understand their low-energy dynamics in ferromagnetic spin chains.
method: A nonperturbative quantization approach is applied to chiral solitons in spin chains, analyzing their condensation into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid.
result: Chiral solitons condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid and appear as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase.
conclusion: The framework provides a way to detect chiral solitons via inelastic neutron scattering, advancing the understanding of soliton dynamics in quantum spin systems.

title: Free And Interacting Fermionic Conformal Field Theories On The Fuzzy Sphere

abstract:

Researchers use noncommutative “fuzzy” spheres to study three-dimensional fermionic conformal field theories, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021055] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses fuzzy sphere regularization to study free and interacting fermionic conformal field theories in three dimensions, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.
motivation: To understand non-perturbative aspects of conformal field theories, particularly fermionic ones, using a noncommutative geometry approach.
method: The authors employ the fuzzy sphere, a noncommutative regularization, to simulate free and interacting fermionic CFTs on a sphere, using numerical techniques.
result: They observe emergent supersymmetry in the interacting theory and compute scaling dimensions and operator spectra.
conclusion: The fuzzy sphere provides a viable non-perturbative tool for studying fermionic CFTs and emergent symmetries.

authors: Paul M. Neves, Takashi Kurumaji, Joshua P. Wakefield, Arno Hiess, Paul Steffens, Navid Qureshi, Robert Cubitt, Lisa M. Debeer-Schmitt, Johanna C. Palmstrom, Satoru Hayami, Marek Bartkowiak, Markus Zolliker, Jonathan S. White, And Joseph G. Checkelsky

authors: Hongwei Zhang, Chunsheng Wang, Ran Wang, Senyang Pan, Hengning Wang, Jiaqiang Cai, Yonglai Liu, Zhe Qu, Xiangde Zhu, Wei Ning, Chuanying Xi, Jinglei Zhang, Ning Hao, Guolin Zheng, And Mingliang Tian

authors: Xiangyu Luo, Ludovica Zullo, Sahaj Patel, Dongjin Oh, Willa Mihalyi-Koch, Emma Lian, Jiaruo Li, Qian Song, Asish K. Kundu, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Elio Vescovo, Natalia Olszowska, Rafał Kurleto, Dawid Wutke, Xavier Roy, Giorgio Sangiovanni, And Riccardo Comin

Systematic corrections to belief propagation enable polynomial-time tensor network contraction algorithms while providing rigorous bounds on approximation errors.

motivation: Tensor network contraction is computationally hard, and belief propagation provides approximate solutions but lacks rigorous error bounds; the authors aim to develop a polynomial-time algorithm with controlled approximation errors.

title: 2d Van Der Waals Magnets: From Fundamental Physics To Applications
authors: Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, And Nuh Gedik
abstract:
Author(s): Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, and Nuh Gedik

Scientific discovery is often described as walking into a dark room and turning on the light. The discovery of 2D magnetism in van der Waals materials in 2016 was one such leap forward, removing one spatial dimension from macroscopic materials. The study of 2D magnets has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena. This review summarizes the current state of knowledge of magnetic phenomena in 2D van der Waals materials. The field encompasses not just the traditional study of ferromagnets and antiferromagnets but also topology, quantum and nonequilibrium dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons and spintronics, and the interaction of magnetism with light, phonons, and electric fields (multiferroics). The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025003] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A review of 2D van der Waals magnets covering fundamental physics and applications.
motivation: To summarize the current state of knowledge and recent discoveries in 2D magnetism, which has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena.
method: The paper is a review that synthesizes experimental and theoretical results on 2D van der Waals magnets, including topics like topology, quantum dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons, and spintronics.
result: The review highlights the rapid progress in understanding 2D magnetism and its potential for applications.
conclusion: The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.

title: Radiation Forces And Torques In Optics And Acoustics
authors: Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, And Konstantin Y. Bliokh
abstract:
Author(s): Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, and Konstantin Y. Bliokh

This review presents a unified perspective of how local energy, momentum, and spin densities in optical and acoustic wave fields induce forces and torques on particles—a topic that has captivated researchers for centuries. Applications discussed include trapping and manipulation of atoms and nanoparticles by light, sorting of biological cells by the combination of acoustics and microfluidics, and pulling forces that draw particles against the direction of wave propagation.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025002] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: A review of radiation forces and torques in optical and acoustic fields, focusing on particle manipulation.
motivation: To provide a unified perspective on how local energy, momentum, and spin densities in wave fields induce forces and torques on particles.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental work on optical and acoustic radiation forces, including trapping, sorting, and pulling effects.
result: Summarizes key principles and applications of radiation forces and torques in optics and acoustics.
conclusion: The field has broad applications in particle manipulation but is not directly related to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review of space-time duality in quantum many-body dynamics, focusing on brickwork quantum circuits.
motivation: Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult; space-time duality offers a unified approach.
method: The review explains how discretizing time evolution on a lattice and treating space and time symmetrically leads to solvable models via brickwork quantum circuits.
result: The paper provides a pedagogical overview of exactly solvable quantum many-body dynamics using space-time duality.
conclusion: Space-time duality and brickwork circuits provide a powerful framework for understanding quantum many-body dynamics, with connections to quantum computation.

title: Kagome Metals
authors: Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, And Stephen D. Wilson
abstract:
Author(s): Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, and Stephen D. Wilson

The kagome lattice is a two-dimensional tiling of hexagons and triangles named after a Japanese basket weaving technique. Its geometry gives rise to highly frustrated interactions and interference effects experienced by electrons and their multiple degrees of freedom. In metals, the exploration of materials with kagome conduction networks is driven by predictions of realizing new electronic states where these interference effects are dominant, amplifying electronic interactions and many-body effects. In these kagome metals, these amplified correlation effects in combination with spin-orbit coupling and other forms of frustration have given rise to a wealth of phenomena beyond expectations. These include unusual states and responses born from topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, sublattice interference effects at saddle points such as unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism and flux phases, amplified anomalous Hall effects, and electronic nematic states. This review examines the theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, with the aim of elucidating fundamental mechanisms underlying the observed exotic phenomena.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015002] Published Thu Feb 12, 2026.
tldr: A review of kagome metals, focusing on exotic electronic states arising from the frustrated lattice geometry.
motivation: To understand the fundamental mechanisms behind unusual phenomena in kagome metals, such as unconventional superconductivity and topological flat bands.
method: The paper reviews theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, synthesizing findings from multiple studies.
result: Kagome metals exhibit a wealth of exotic phenomena including topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, and unconventional superconductivity.
conclusion: The kagome lattice provides a rich platform for studying strongly correlated and topological electronic states.

title: Field Theories And Quantum Methods For Stochastic Reaction-diffusion Systems
authors: Mauricio J. Del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, And Wout Merbis
abstract:
Author(s): Mauricio J. del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, and Wout Merbis

The exchange of energy and molecules in a living cell, the spread of opinions through a society, and the flow of traffic in a crowded city are very different phenomena, yet they are all examples of complex systems composed of many agents that interact with each other and exchange energy or particles with the environment. These systems can be modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems. In this pedagogical review, the authors apply powerful field-theoretic methods to these systems, unifying diverse approaches under a single framework. The methods are useful for handling chemical systems but also have applications in a wide range of areas such as ecology and epidemiology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015001] Published Thu Jan 22, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review applying field-theoretic methods to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems in biology, ecology, and epidemiology.
motivation: To unify diverse approaches for modeling complex systems with many interacting agents using field theories.
method: The authors review and apply field-theoretic methods, such as Doi-Peliti formalism and path integrals, to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems.
result: The review demonstrates how field theories provide a powerful framework for analyzing these systems, with applications beyond chemistry.
conclusion: Field-theoretic methods are valuable for studying stochastic reaction-diffusion systems across multiple disciplines.

title: Spin-glass Dynamics: Experiment, Theory, And Simulation
authors: E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, And D. Yllanes
abstract:
Author(s): E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, and D. Yllanes

This review updates the field of spin glasses with broad application to a large variety of physical systems. In particular, this review tracks the progress of experiment, theory, and large-scale simulations. It highlights the importance of their synergy, from the inception of the field to the present day, and includes future opportunities for research.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045005] Published Mon Dec 15, 2025.
tldr: A review of spin-glass dynamics covering experiment, theory, and simulation.
motivation: To provide an updated overview of spin-glass research and highlight the synergy between experimental, theoretical, and computational approaches.
method: Review of experimental techniques, theoretical models, and large-scale simulations of spin glasses.
result: Summarizes key advances in understanding spin-glass dynamics and identifies future research opportunities.
conclusion: Spin-glass dynamics remain a rich field with broad applications, and continued interdisciplinary collaboration is essential.

title: Kitaev Quantum Spin Liquids
authors: Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, And Hae-Young Kee
abstract:
Author(s): Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, and Hae-Young Kee

Frustration in spin systems can prevent ordering even at =0, creating quantum spin liquids that have been sought since Anderson’s pioneering work in 1973 and his influential 1987 paper connecting them to high-temperature superconductivity. Kitaev’s solvable spin-1/2 models on a honeycomb lattice brought renewed attention to this field, with Jackeli and Khaliullin later revealing how to engineer Kitaev interactions in real materials. This review highlights theoretical and experimental developments in Kitaev spin liquids, emphasizing leading candidate materials and their broad topological properties such as chiral edge modes. Consequently, it provides essential insights for both experimentalists and theorists working on quantum spin liquid problems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045003] Published Wed Dec 03, 2025.
tldr: A review of Kitaev quantum spin liquids, focusing on candidate materials and topological properties.
motivation: To provide an overview of theoretical and experimental progress in Kitaev spin liquids, which are a type of quantum spin liquid with potential applications in topological quantum computing.
method: The paper reviews theoretical models (Kitaev honeycomb model) and experimental realizations in materials, highlighting chiral edge modes and other topological features.
result: The review summarizes key candidate materials and their properties, emphasizing the broad topological phenomena observed.
conclusion: Kitaev spin liquids remain an active area of research with promising directions for future study, particularly in material synthesis and characterization.

title: The Ups And Downs Of Internal Conversion
authors: Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, And Salvy P. Russo
abstract:
Author(s): Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, and Salvy P. Russo

This review examines the theoretical methods used to describe the photophysical process of internal conversion in quantum systems. These models explore all facets of the nonradiative mechanism, and the review presents an outlook on how they can be incorporated in studies relevant to applications, for example, in photonics and energy harvesting.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035003] Published Tue Sep 16, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical methods for internal conversion in quantum systems, focusing on nonradiative transitions and their applications in photonics and energy harvesting.
motivation: Internal conversion is a fundamental photophysical process, and understanding its theoretical underpinnings is important for applications in photonics and energy harvesting.
method: The paper reviews various theoretical models for internal conversion, including nonradiative decay mechanisms and their incorporation into studies of quantum systems.
result: The review provides an overview of current theoretical methods and an outlook on their application to photonics and energy harvesting.
conclusion: Theoretical methods for internal conversion are well-developed and can be applied to practical applications, but the paper does not present new results or directly advance quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Colloquium: Quantum Properties And Functionalities Of Magnetic Skyrmions
authors: Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, And Christos Panagopoulos
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, and Christos Panagopoulos

Skyrmions are topological field configurations that were first discussed in the context of high-energy theory. In recent years, skyrmionic spin patterns in solid-state systems have received much attention, in part for their promising application potential. This Colloquium discusses quantum-mechanical aspects of such magnetic skyrmions, both for the interactions that underlie skyrmion formation and for quantum features of the skyrmions themselves.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 031001] Published Tue Jul 08, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews quantum properties and functionalities of magnetic skyrmions, focusing on their topological nature and potential applications.
motivation: Magnetic skyrmions are promising for future spintronic devices, and understanding their quantum aspects is crucial for advancing both fundamental physics and applications.
method: The paper surveys theoretical and experimental work on skyrmion formation, quantum features, and interactions, providing a comprehensive overview.
result: It highlights quantum-mechanical effects in skyrmion systems, such as quantum tunneling and entanglement, and discusses their potential for quantum information processing.
conclusion: Magnetic skyrmions exhibit rich quantum behavior that could be harnessed for novel quantum technologies, but the field is still in early stages.

title: Spin-dependent Exotic Interactions
authors: Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, And Dmitry Budker
abstract:
Author(s): Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, and Dmitry Budker

This review presents a comprehensive summary of theoretical investigations and experimental searches for spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model. These interactions may be mediated by various types of exotic bosons, and their existence and properties may, in turn, explain the nature of dark matter and dark energy. The described experiments also probe the discrete fundamental symmetries of nature.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025005] Published Tue Jun 24, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental searches for spin-dependent exotic interactions beyond the standard model, including their possible connection to dark matter and dark energy.
motivation: To understand the nature of dark matter and dark energy and to test fundamental symmetries of nature through spin-dependent interactions mediated by exotic bosons.
method: The paper surveys theoretical models of spin-dependent exotic interactions and reviews experimental techniques used to search for them, such as precision measurements with atomic, molecular, and optical systems.
result: The review summarizes current constraints on various spin-dependent interactions and highlights the potential of ongoing and future experiments to discover new physics.
conclusion: Spin-dependent exotic interactions provide a promising avenue for probing physics beyond the standard model, and further experimental and theoretical work is needed to fully explore their implications.

title: Quantum Physics Of Stars
authors: M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. Deboer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, And A. Tumino
abstract:
Author(s): M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. deBoer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, and A. Tumino

There are many nuclear reactions that are of central importance for stellar burning and element formation. In typical stars, these reactions take place at very low energy, and many of them have very small rates, making it difficult to measure them directly in the laboratory. On the theoretical side, the low-energy regime is governed by quantum-mechanical phenomena like tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects. This review summarizes the state of the art in the theory of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars and describes new ideas for studying these reactions on Earth.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025003] Published Tue May 27, 2025.
tldr: This review summarizes the state of the art in low-energy nuclear reactions in stars, focusing on quantum tunneling, resonances, and interference effects.
motivation: Nuclear reactions at stellar energies are difficult to measure directly due to very small rates, yet they are crucial for understanding stellar burning and nucleosynthesis.
method: The paper reviews theoretical approaches including quantum-mechanical tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects, and discusses new experimental ideas.
result: It provides a comprehensive overview of current theoretical methods and experimental challenges in low-energy nuclear astrophysics.
conclusion: Advances in theory and experiment are needed to better understand stellar nuclear reactions, which are governed by quantum phenomena.

title: Colloquium: Materials That Exceed Classical Thermodynamic Bounds On Properties
authors: Roderic S. Lakes
abstract:
Author(s): Roderic S. Lakes

Classical thermodynamic bounds provide constraints on values that are expected in measurements of certain physical properties. In a variety of fields, some measurements exceed these bounds. This apparent violation of thermodynamics arises because the measurements are made in ways that violate the underlying assumptions made when deriving these bounds. This Colloquium describes a wide variety of circumstances where such violations occur and which of the underlying assumptions are violated in each case. It also describes how interesting material properties can be developed using materials designed to violate these assumptions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021002] Published Wed May 14, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews materials that appear to exceed classical thermodynamic bounds on properties, explaining the violations by examining underlying assumptions.
motivation: To clarify why certain measurements exceed classical thermodynamic bounds and to show how materials can be designed to exploit these violations.
method: The paper surveys a wide variety of examples from different fields where measured properties exceed classical bounds, and analyzes which assumptions of the bounds are violated.
result: It identifies that violations occur because measurements are made in ways that violate assumptions such as equilibrium, linearity, or homogeneity, and demonstrates how designed materials can achieve extreme properties.
conclusion: Understanding the assumptions behind thermodynamic bounds allows for the design of materials with properties that surpass conventional limits, without violating thermodynamics.

title: Colloquium: Synthetic Quantum Matter In Nonstandard Geometries
authors: Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, And Christof Weitenberg
abstract:
Author(s): Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, and Christof Weitenberg

This Colloquium presents ways to implement fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems. The study of quantum many-body physics in these exotic geometries permits simulation of phenomena from topology in condensed matter to models of gravity and cosmology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 011001] Published Tue Mar 25, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review on implementing fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems for quantum many-body physics.
motivation: To explore quantum many-body physics in nonstandard geometries, enabling simulation of phenomena from condensed matter topology to gravity and cosmology.
method: Reviews experimental and theoretical approaches for realizing fractal lattices, curved spaces, and synthetic dimensions in cold atoms, photonics, and electronic systems.
result: Summarizes recent progress in engineering exotic geometries and their potential for simulating topological phases and gravitational analogs.
conclusion: Synthetic quantum matter in nonstandard geometries is a rapidly advancing field with connections to condensed matter and high-energy physics, but it does not directly address the user's specified research directions.

title: Massive Quantum Systems As Interfaces Of Quantum Mechanics And Gravity
authors: Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, And Clara C. Wanjura
abstract:
Author(s): Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, and Clara C. Wanjura

The authors review theories and experimental state-of-the-art efforts to study the effects of gravity on massive quantum systems. Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force and may be addressed via precision quantum probes. Experiments testing whether the quantum nature of gravity causes decoherence and collapse of matter-wave functions and whether it can mediate entanglement between separate massive particles are underway, and their results will guide the theoretical description of gravity effects on a laboratory scale.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015003] Published Thu Feb 13, 2025.
tldr: A review of experimental and theoretical efforts to probe gravity using massive quantum systems, focusing on decoherence and entanglement mediated by gravity.
motivation: Classical gravity is the least precisely tested fundamental force, and quantum probes may reveal its quantum nature.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks (e.g., decoherence models, entanglement tests) and experimental platforms (e.g., matter-wave interferometry, optomechanics) for testing gravity with massive quantum systems.
result: Current experiments are approaching the sensitivity needed to test whether gravity induces decoherence or entanglement, but no definitive results have been obtained yet.
conclusion: Massive quantum systems offer a promising avenue to study the interplay between quantum mechanics and gravity, guiding future theoretical and experimental work.

title: Pilot-Wave Simulator: Exact Classical Sampling From Ideal And Noisy Quantum Circuits Up To Hundreds Of Qubits
authors: Gleb Kalachev, Pavel Mosharev, Zuoheng Zou, Pavel Panteleev, And Man-Hong Yung
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2173 (2026).

Quantum circuit simulators running on classical computers offer a vital platform for designing, testing, and optimizing quantum algorithms, driving innovation despite limited access to real quantum hardware. However, their scalability is inherently constrained by exponential memory and computational overhead, which restricts accurate simulation of large-scale quantum circuits and often results in approximate output distributions. Here, we propose an exact sampling algorithm that integrates tensor network contraction techniques with a Markov process, wherein a classical state evolves according to the local structure of the quantum circuit. As a demonstration, we target the challenge of generating samples from ideal and noisy QAOA circuits with up to 476 qubits, incorporating both depolarizing and amplitude damping noise models. These results enable further validation of several assumptions and conjectures at a scale previously out of reach, significantly expanding the scope of classical simulation in quantum algorithm research.

.
tldr: This paper presents a classical algorithm for exact sampling from quantum circuits using tensor network contraction and Markov processes, demonstrated on QAOA circuits with up to 476 qubits.
motivation: Classical simulation of quantum circuits is essential for testing quantum algorithms but faces exponential overhead; the authors aim to extend exact sampling to larger circuits than previously possible.
method: The algorithm integrates tensor network contraction techniques with a Markov process where a classical state evolves according to the local structure of the quantum circuit.
result: They demonstrate exact sampling from ideal and noisy QAOA circuits with up to 476 qubits, incorporating depolarizing and amplitude damping noise models.
conclusion: This work expands the scope of classical simulation for quantum algorithm research, enabling validation of assumptions at a larger scale.

title: On The Significance Of Wigner’s Friend In Contexts Beyond Quantum Foundations
authors: Caroline L. Jones And Markus P. Mueller
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2147 (2026).

There has been a surge of recent interest in the Wigner's Friend paradox, sparking several novel thought experiments and no-go theorems. The main narrative has been that Wigner's Friend highlights a counterintuitive feature that is unique to quantum theory, and which is closely related to the quantum measurement problem. Here, we challenge this view. We argue that the gist of the Wigner's Friend paradox can be reproduced without assuming quantum physics, and that it underlies a much broader class of enigmas in the foundations of physics and philosophy. To show this, we first consider several recently proposed Extended Wigner's Friend scenarios, and demonstrate that some of their implications for the absoluteness of observations can be reproduced by classical thought experiments that involve the duplication of agents. Crucially, some of these classical scenarios are technologically much easier to implement than their quantum counterparts. Then, we argue that the essential structural ingredient of all these scenarios is a feature that we call "Restriction A": that a physical theory cannot give us a probabilistic description of the observations of all agents. Finally, we argue that this difficulty is at the core of other puzzles in the foundations of physics and philosophy, and demonstrate this explicitly for cosmology's Boltzmann brain problem. Our analysis suggests that Wigner's Friend should be studied in a larger context, addressing a frontier of human knowledge beyond quantum foundations: to obtain reliable predictions for experiments in which these predictions can be privately but not intersubjectively verified.

.
tldr: The paper argues that the Wigner's Friend paradox is not unique to quantum theory but can be reproduced classically, and relates it to broader foundational puzzles.
motivation: To challenge the view that Wigner's Friend highlights a uniquely quantum feature and to show its relevance to other foundational problems.
method: The authors construct classical thought experiments that mimic extended Wigner's Friend scenarios and identify a common structural feature called 'Restriction A'.
result: They demonstrate that some implications of Wigner's Friend can be reproduced classically, and that the paradox shares structure with the Boltzmann brain problem.
conclusion: Wigner's Friend should be studied in a broader context beyond quantum foundations, addressing issues of private vs. intersubjective verification.

title: Superluminal Transformations And Indeterminism
authors: Amrapali Sen And Flavio Del Santo
abstract: Quantum theory is widely regarded as fundamentally indeterministic, yet classical frameworks can also exhibit indeterminism once infinite information is abandoned. At the same time, relativity is usually taken to forbid superluminal signalling, although Lorentz symmetry formally admits superluminal transformations (SpTs). Dragan and Ekert have argued that SpTs entail a form of indeterminism analogous to that encountered in quantum theory. Here, we derive a theory-independent no-go theorem from a set of natural assumptions: any framework admitting non-order-preserving SpTs must either abandon finite information, relinquish time-symmetric informational content, deny that the past stores memory, or abandon the notion that time determines a preferred causal ordering. In particular, one possible implication is that any theory accommodating SpTs suggests an ontology with unbounded informational content, akin to deterministic classical theories formulated over the real numbers. Consequently, any ontic indeterminacy associated with superluminal transformations cannot originate from finite information.
tldr: This paper explores the connection between superluminal transformations and indeterminism, deriving a no-go theorem that challenges the idea that finite information can explain quantum-like indeterminism.
motivation: To understand whether superluminal transformations can provide a classical explanation for quantum indeterminism, as suggested by Dragan and Ekert.
method: The authors derive a theory-independent no-go theorem from natural assumptions about time ordering, information content, and memory.
result: Any theory admitting non-order-preserving superluminal transformations must either abandon finite information, relinquish time-symmetric informational content, deny that the past stores memory, or abandon time-determined causal ordering.
conclusion: Ontic indeterminacy associated with superluminal transformations cannot originate from finite information, implying that such theories require unbounded informational content.

title: Wave Packet Motion In A Quantized Electromagnetic Field: Analytic Results
authors: Szabolcs Hack, Béla Gábor Pusztai, Krisztina Joós, Sándor Varró, Attila Czirják And Péter Földi
abstract: We investigate the dynamics of a charged particle interacting with a multimode quantized electromagnetic field and obtain an analytic solution for the full electron-field system. In the present finite-mode formulation the total electron-field dynamics remains closed and unitary. The framework enables the calculation of position expectation values and uncertainties for arbitrary wave packets and field states, allowing us to identify quantum corrections to the corresponding classical motion. While the corrections to the position expectation value are weak and largely insensitive to the quantum state of the field, the wave packet broadening exhibits a pronounced dependence on the field state. In particular, the quantum uncertainty of the radiation is directly imprinted onto the spatial uncertainty of the particle. We illustrate these effects for Gaussian wave packets interacting with coherent, Fock, and squeezed states, including bright squeezed vacuum. The interaction with a finite-duration laser pulse is also analyzed as a multimode example. Our results provide a transparent analytic route toward understanding how quantum fluctuations of light influence electron dynamics in strong-field settings.
tldr: This paper analytically solves the dynamics of a charged particle interacting with a multimode quantized electromagnetic field, showing how quantum field fluctuations affect electron motion.
motivation: Understanding how quantum fluctuations of light influence electron dynamics in strong-field settings is important for fundamental physics and applications like attosecond science.
method: The authors obtain an analytic solution for the full electron-field system in a finite-mode formulation, computing position expectation values and uncertainties for arbitrary wave packets and field states.
result: Quantum corrections to the position expectation value are weak and largely field-state independent, but wave packet broadening strongly depends on the field state, with quantum uncertainty of radiation imprinted onto spatial uncertainty of the particle.
conclusion: The results provide a transparent analytic route to understanding quantum light effects on electron dynamics, with potential implications for strong-field physics and quantum optics.

title: Observation Of Alignment Tensor Effects In Metastability-exchange Collisions With Highly Polarized 3 ...
authors: Yida Sha, Kaiwen Yi, Xingqing Jin, Matteo Fadel And Xiang Peng
abstract: Highly polarized ensembles prepared by metastability-exchange optical pumping (MEOP) have been widely used in precision measurements and fundamental physics. Metastability-exchange (ME) collisions, serving as the basis of MEOP, are traditionally described in terms of atomic orientation, while the significant contributions of metastable alignment tensor at high polarization remain unexplored. In this work, we develop a linearized model under mean-field approximation to investigate alignment tensor effects in highly polarized , which originate from the metastable manifold and are revealed through ME-induced relaxation and frequency shift. By means of free-induction-decay measurements, a pronounced dependence on nuclear polarization is experimentally observed in the response of the ground-state-metastable hybrid ensembles to the external magnetic field. Furthermore, after obtaining the characteristics of tensor-induced phenomena, we demonstrate good agreement between the experiment and the theory. This work advances the understanding of nuclear spin dynamics in highly polarized using MEOP. It further provides applications in systematic error correction of high-accuracy magnetometry, as well as in optimal protocol for the generation of nuclear spin-squeezed states.
tldr: This paper studies alignment tensor effects in metastability-exchange collisions with highly polarized 3He, focusing on nuclear spin dynamics and applications to magnetometry.
motivation: To understand alignment tensor contributions in highly polarized 3He ensembles, which are not captured by traditional orientation-based models, and to improve precision measurements.
method: A linearized mean-field model is developed to describe alignment tensor effects, and free-induction-decay measurements are performed to observe the dependence on nuclear polarization.
result: A pronounced dependence on nuclear polarization is observed in the ground-state-metastable hybrid ensemble's response to magnetic fields, and good agreement between experiment and theory is demonstrated.
conclusion: The work advances understanding of nuclear spin dynamics in highly polarized 3He and provides applications for systematic error correction in magnetometry and generation of spin-squeezed states.

title: Non-spreading Meronic Spin Defects Around Optical Vortices
authors: Miguel A Porras And Yijie Shen Nilo Mata-Cervera
abstract: Optical vortices are singularity lines where the light field intensity vanishes and its phase is undefined. These threads of darkness are adorned by Gauss’s law as lines of pure longitudinal polarization where the polarization plane tilts and winds around. The resulting spin field is as a unique structure with both features of topological texture and defect, as it includes a point defect of undefined spin enclosed by a meronic texture which spans half the spin unit sphere. This topological structure does not spread in propagation: the normalized spin field maintains a deep-subwavelength confinement around the vortex line while the underlying vortex beam continues to diffract. From their intrinsic nature and subwavelength confinement, these textures exhibit enhanced robustness upon isotropic perturbations such as atmospheric turbulence compared with other tailored polarization textures. Here we describe these topologies of transverse spin which decorate the phase singularity of paraxial vortex beams, highlighting the diversity of topological structures that arise in two different spaces—the spin unit sphere and the transverse-axial Poincaré sphere—and discuss the underlying aspects behind their subwavelength localization.
tldr: This paper studies topological spin textures around optical vortices, focusing on meronic defects and subwavelength confinement.
motivation: To understand and characterize the unique topological spin structures that decorate phase singularities in paraxial vortex beams.
method: Theoretical analysis of the spin field around optical vortices, using concepts from topology and polarization optics.
result: The spin field exhibits a meronic texture with a point defect, remains non-spreading and subwavelength confined, and shows enhanced robustness against perturbations.
conclusion: These topological spin structures are intrinsic to optical vortices and have potential applications in robust optical manipulation and information transfer.

title: Observation Of Floquet Tensor Monopoles
authors: Hao Yuan, Weixuan Zhang, Na Sun And Xiangdong Zhang
abstract: Tensor monopoles, topological singularities of Kalb–Ramond tensor gauge fields, have garnered widespread attention in high-energy and condensed matter physics. They give rise to exotic phenomena such as quantized magnetoelectric responses and chiral boundary states, acting as potential building blocks for the development of topological devices in high-dimensional space. However, theoretical studies and experimental realizations reported to date have remained in static settings, and the realization of Floquet tensor monopoles (FTMs) and their associated anomalous non-equilibrium topological features has yet to be achieved. Here, we report the first theoretical and experimental implementation of FTMs in a four-dimensional non-equilibrium system. We systematically uncover the driving-frequency controlled creation, motion, and annihilation of FTMs, together with their anomalous bulk-edge correspondence. These phenomena are unique to FTMs and have no static counterparts. In experiments, we design and fabricate time-varying topological circuits, and directly observe the controllable motion of FTMs in k-space and their induced 3D Fermi-arc surface states by tuning the driving frequency. Our findings extend tensor monopole research to the non-equilibrium regime, providing a theoretical and experimental platform for exploring exotic topological phases in dynamic tensor gauge fields and laying the groundwork for functional topological devices with real-time control.
tldr: This paper reports the first experimental observation of Floquet tensor monopoles in a four-dimensional non-equilibrium system, demonstrating controllable creation, motion, and annihilation of tensor monopoles and their anomalous bulk-edge correspondence.
motivation: Tensor monopoles have been studied in static settings, but their non-equilibrium (Floquet) counterparts and associated topological features have not been realized, limiting potential applications in dynamic topological devices.
method: The authors design and fabricate time-varying topological circuits to realize a four-dimensional non-equilibrium system, and directly observe the motion of Floquet tensor monopoles in momentum space and their induced 3D Fermi-arc surface states by tuning the driving frequency.
result: They systematically uncover driving-frequency controlled creation, motion, and annihilation of Floquet tensor monopoles, along with anomalous bulk-edge correspondence that has no static counterpart.
conclusion: This work extends tensor monopole research to the non-equilibrium regime, providing a platform for exploring exotic topological phases in dynamic tensor gauge fields and laying groundwork for functional topological devices with real-time control.

title: A Less-for-more Metamaterial Paradigm Via Laplace-Helmholtz Correspondence
authors: Zihang Guo, Fubao Yang, Tong Li, Shuihua Yang, Cheng-Wei Qiu, Jingjing He And Liujun Xu
abstract: The Laplace and Helmholtz equations dominate two fundamentally distinct physical processes: steady diffusion with a single constitutive parameter versus dynamic wave propagation with two. Manipulating complex wave dynamics through simple steady fields is typically deemed infeasible. Here, we bridge this gap by establishing the Laplace-Helmholtz correspondence, enabling a ‘less-for-more’ paradigm for metamaterial design. Rooted in a wave invariant, this framework allows the rigorous derivation of the two parameters and oscillatory field for the Helmholtz equation (the ‘more’) solely from the single parameter and steady field of the Laplace equation (the ‘less’). We demonstrate this capability by unlocking functionalities previously considered intractable, such as hyperbolic invisibility and three-dimensional freeform conformal cloaking with broadband performance. We further experimentally validate our strategy via a waveguide cloak. Our results bridge static and dynamic physics, establishing a versatile gateway for manipulating waves beyond conventional constraints.
tldr: This paper establishes a mathematical correspondence between Laplace and Helmholtz equations to design metamaterials for wave manipulation using static diffusion parameters.
motivation: To bridge the gap between static and dynamic physics, enabling complex wave functionalities (e.g., cloaking) through simpler steady-field design.
method: The authors derive a wave invariant that maps the single-parameter Laplace equation to the two-parameter Helmholtz equation, allowing wave field reconstruction from static solutions.
result: They demonstrate hyperbolic invisibility and 3D freeform conformal cloaking with broadband performance, validated experimentally with a waveguide cloak.
conclusion: The Laplace-Helmholtz correspondence provides a versatile gateway for manipulating waves beyond conventional constraints, with potential applications in metamaterial design.

title: A Comprehensive Review On Master Stability Functions In Complex Network Dynamics
authors: Priodyuti Pradhan And Chandrakala Meena Suman Acharyya
abstract: Synchronization is a fundamental emergent phenomenon observed across a wide range of natural and engineered systems. Understanding the stability of a synchronization phenomenon is crucial for ensuring functionality in various complex systems. The master stability function (MSF) framework has emerged as a powerful and elegant tool for analyzing the stability of synchronization in coupled dynamical systems. By separating the effects of the node dynamics from the network structure, the MSF offers deep insights into synchronization behavior. However, a major challenge lies in determining the MSF for complex dynamical networks driven by nonlinear interaction mechanisms. These mechanisms introduce additional complexity due to the intricate connectivity of the interacting elements and the complex dynamics governed by nonlinear processes, diverse parameters, and the higher dimensionality of the system. Although MSF analysis has been widely used for more than past 25 years, a comprehensive and systematic investigation of MSF across various networked systems is still lacking. In this article, we present a simplified and unified analysis for the MSF in various undirected and directed networked systems. We begin by formulating the MSF framework in pairwise coupled identical systems and extend our analysis to directed networks and multilayer networks, considering both intralayer and interlayer interactions. Furthermore, we analyze the MSF formalism for higher-order networks. To facilitate understanding, we complement the theoretical developments with numerical analysis of synchronization stability in coupled systems. We also propose algorithms for computing the MSF, identifying stability regimes, and classifying the MSF behaviors. Overall, the primary goal of this review is to present a systematic study of the MSF in various coupled dynamical networks in a clear and structured manner, making this powerful tool more accessible. Furthermore, we highlight underexplored areas in the application of the MSF and discuss emerging directions, such as estimating the MSF using machine learning approaches.
tldr: A comprehensive review of master stability functions for synchronization in complex networks, covering pairwise, directed, multilayer, and higher-order networks.
motivation: Synchronization is a fundamental phenomenon in natural and engineered systems, and understanding its stability is crucial. The master stability function (MSF) is a powerful tool, but a systematic investigation across various networked systems is lacking.
method: The authors formulate the MSF framework for pairwise coupled identical systems, then extend to directed networks, multilayer networks (intra- and interlayer), and higher-order networks. They complement theory with numerical analysis and propose algorithms for computing MSF and classifying stability regimes.
result: A unified and simplified MSF analysis is presented for various network types, with numerical demonstrations and algorithms for stability regime identification.
conclusion: The review provides a systematic study of MSF in complex dynamical networks, making the tool more accessible, and highlights underexplored areas and future directions like machine learning for MSF estimation.

title: Classification And Correlation Signatures Of Chiral Spin Liquids On The Pyrochlore Lattice
authors: Leon Balents And Yasir Iqbal Chunxiao Liu
abstract: We present a systematic classification and variational study of chiral quantum spin liquids on the pyrochlore lattice based on fermionic parton constructions. Focusing on chiral and spin-liquid Ansätze, we characterize their symmetry properties, flux structures, and low-energy spinon spectra within a projective symmetry group framework, and incorporate gauge fluctuations through Gutzwiller-projected wave functions studied by variational Monte Carlo. From the equal-time spin structure factor, we develop correlation-based diagnostics that distinguish gauge-dominated Coulomb phases from states with substantial matter-field and short-range contributions. Distinct chiral flux sectors, though close in energy, exhibit markedly different degrees of emergent gauge-field dominance, reflected in the geometry and contrast of pinch-point singularities. Although these states are not competitive ground states of the nearest-neighbor Heisenberg model, they define a physically meaningful family of proximate chiral phases relevant to extended pyrochlore Hamiltonians.
tldr: This paper classifies chiral spin liquids on the pyrochlore lattice using parton constructions and variational Monte Carlo, focusing on symmetry and flux structures.
motivation: Chiral spin liquids are exotic quantum phases, but the paper's focus on pyrochlore lattice classification and correlation signatures does not align with the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.
method: The authors use fermionic parton constructions, projective symmetry group analysis, and Gutzwiller-projected wave functions with variational Monte Carlo to study chiral spin liquid Ansätze.
result: They identify distinct chiral flux sectors with different degrees of gauge-field dominance, reflected in pinch-point singularities in the spin structure factor.
conclusion: These chiral phases are not ground states of the nearest-neighbor Heisenberg model but are relevant to extended pyrochlore Hamiltonians.

title: Construction And Dynamic Update Of Channel Gain Maps Via 3d Gaussian Splatting
authors: Yilong Chen, Yuan Guo, Juncong Zhou, Jie Xu, Rui Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.21099v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Channel knowledge maps (CKMs) have emerged as a promising technique for providing scene-specific and location-dependent propagation knowledge to enable environment-aware wireless network design. This paper investigates the construction and dynamic updating of a particular type of CKM, namely grid-based channel gain maps (CGMs), for large-scale networks using three-dimensional Gaussian splatting (3DGS). First, we formulate a grid-based channel gain model, where each map entry is defined as the locally averaged channel gain over a receiver grid, thereby suppressing phase-sensitive small-scale fluctuations. The resulting channel gain is decomposed into distance-dependent attenuation, path transmittance, and effective scattering contributions. Based on this decomposition, we develop a physics-informed Gaussian-splatting-based channel gain (GS-CG) model, which represents the propagation environment as a set of Gaussian primitives. The proposed model maps Gaussian geometry, opacity, and directional features to propagation-related factors and renders grid-level channel gains through a differentiable process. To accommodate real-time environmental changes, we further propose an incremental learning mechanism that updates a static reference GS-CG representation into a dynamic CGM. Specifically, the reference Gaussian primitives are frozen, while a compact set of tunable Gaussians is introduced to capture newly induced local channel-gain variations from sparse measurements.Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed GS-CG methods accurately reconstruct grid-based CGMs, efficiently adapt to dynamic environmental changes, and achieve a favorable accuracy-complexity tradeoff for fast CGM refinement.
tldr: This paper uses 3D Gaussian splatting to construct and dynamically update channel gain maps for wireless communication networks.
motivation: Channel knowledge maps (CKMs) are needed for environment-aware wireless network design, but existing methods lack efficient dynamic updating for large-scale networks.
method: A physics-informed Gaussian-splatting-based channel gain (GS-CG) model is proposed, representing the propagation environment as Gaussian primitives and rendering grid-level channel gains via differentiable rendering; an incremental learning mechanism updates the model with sparse measurements.
result: The proposed GS-CG methods accurately reconstruct grid-based channel gain maps and efficiently adapt to dynamic environmental changes with favorable accuracy-complexity tradeoff.
conclusion: 3D Gaussian splatting is effective for constructing and updating channel gain maps, enabling fast CGM refinement for wireless networks.

title: Exact Ensemble Controllability For Neural Differential Equations Via Neural Interpolation
authors: Martin Gugat
abstract: ArXiv:2607.21112v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a system that is governed by neural dynamics. Neural dynamics are a model for deep neural networks with a large number of layers. For a differential equation where the right-hand side is given by a neural network, we analyze the exact ensemble controllability of the system. This property plays an essential role in Machine Learning. It concerns the ability to learn to perform different tasks simultaneously with a single neural dynamics: Exact ensemble controllability requires that [MATH] different initial states are steered to corresponding [MATH] target states with a single set of control parameters. We present a constructive solution to the problem. The construction is based on the solution of a neural interpolation problem. We show that if the right-hand side of the differential equation is given by a neural network of depth two, the interpolation problem can be reduced to the solution of a system of linear equations.
tldr: This paper studies exact ensemble controllability for neural differential equations using neural interpolation, which is a topic in machine learning and control theory, not quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The ability to steer multiple initial states to target states with a single set of control parameters is essential for multi-task learning in deep neural networks.
method: The paper reduces the controllability problem to a neural interpolation problem and shows that for a depth-two neural network, the interpolation reduces to solving a linear system.
result: A constructive solution for exact ensemble controllability is provided, demonstrating that a single neural dynamics can simultaneously perform multiple tasks.
conclusion: The work contributes to the theoretical foundations of neural network training but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: A Log-majorization Inequality For Normal Matrices With Applications To Determinantal Inequalities And Geometric Means
authors: Mohammad Mahdi Ghabries
abstract: ArXiv:2607.21163v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a log-majorization inequality comparing the eigenvalues of the interlaced product [MATH] with those of [MATH], valid for every positive semi-definite [MATH] and every normal [MATH], with the inequality reversing for [MATH] when [MATH] is positive definite. This extends known Hermitian results to the strictly larger class of normal matrices, where normality is shown to be the exact structural hypothesis, not a technical convenience. A counterexample proves the result can fail without it. As applications, we settle a normal-matrix extension of a determinantal conjecture of Lin, proving $[MATH][MATH]A[MATH]B[MATH]p \ge 0$, and we give a complete eigenvalue picture for products of weighted geometric means, sharpening and complementing a theorem of Hiai and Lin.
tldr: This paper proves a log-majorization inequality for normal matrices and applies it to determinantal inequalities and geometric means.
motivation: Extend known Hermitian matrix inequalities to the larger class of normal matrices, settling a conjecture of Lin.
method: Uses matrix analysis and majorization theory, with counterexamples to show necessity of normality.
result: Establishes the log-majorization inequality and proves a normal-matrix extension of Lin's determinantal conjecture.
conclusion: Normality is the exact structural hypothesis for the inequality, and the results sharpen prior work on geometric means.

title: A Kuramoto Phase Model To Explore The Synchronisation Of A Network Of Circadian Clocks
authors: Franck Delaunay (IBV), Antoine Fortun\'e (IBV), Ines Krawczyk (IBV), Mar\'echal Anastasia (maiage), Mathieu Mezache (maiage, MUSCA), Laurent Tournier
abstract: ArXiv:2607.21214v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a model of the circadian clock in a population of cells based on a network of oscillators, derived from the Kuramoto model. The coupling between oscillators is described by a global interaction term but we introduce a phase-dependent coupling mechanism, such that oscillators interact only within a specific interval of the cycle corresponding to a specific stage of the circadian cycle. We analytically demonstrate that this modified system achieves complete asymptotic phase synchronisation, provided specific conditions on the initial phase distribution and the coupling window length are met. To bridge this theoretical framework with experimental observations, we introduce a signal processing procedure based on wavelet decomposition to extract quantitative oscillatory features from Per2::luciferase reporter traces. We then calibrate the model against datasets from both wild type and Cry2 knockout hepatocyte spheroids using a two-step quasi-Monte Carlo filtering algorithm. The comparative analysis reveals significant phenotypic divergence, showing that the Cry2KO condition alters the identifiability landscape of the model's parameters and introduces new compensatory mechanisms that confound the initial population heterogeneity with long-term macroscopic signal decay.
tldr: This paper models circadian clock synchronization in cell populations using a modified Kuramoto model with phase-dependent coupling, calibrated against experimental data.
motivation: Understanding synchronization of circadian clocks in cell populations is important for chronobiology, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: A Kuramoto model with phase-dependent coupling is analyzed analytically for synchronization conditions, and a wavelet-based signal processing procedure is used to calibrate the model against Per2::luciferase reporter data from wild-type and Cry2 knockout hepatocyte spheroids.
result: Complete asymptotic phase synchronization is achieved under specific conditions; Cry2 knockout alters parameter identifiability and introduces compensatory mechanisms.
conclusion: The model captures phenotypic differences in circadian rhythms, but the work is purely classical and biological, with no quantum or information-theoretic content.

title: 3d Uncertainty Quantification For The Photo-Acoustic Tomography
authors: Babak Maboudi Afkham, Amal Mohammed A Alghami, Hassan Yazdanian, Tanja Tarvainen
abstract: ArXiv:2607.21373v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Photoacoustic tomography (PAT) is a promising modality for high-resolution biomedical imaging, motivating the need for reliable uncertainty quantification (UQ) of reconstructed images. Bayesian approaches provide a rigorous framework for UQ but remain computationally challenging for realistic three-dimensional PAT and are sensitive to numerical approximations in the governing wave equation. We develop a finite-element Bayesian UQ framework for PAT that accommodates complex computational domains and detector geometries while enabling large-scale three-dimensional inference. The proposed methodology reformulates the randomize-then-optimize (RTO) sampling strategy as a matrix-free algorithm that generates independent posterior samples using only forward and adjoint wave propagations. Particular attention is given to constructing an adjoint discretization that forms an exact transpose pair with the discrete forward operator while remaining consistent with the continuous PAT adjoint, enabling efficient least-squares solvers within the sampling procedure. We investigate the influence of temporal discretization, artificial boundary conditions, and adjoint consistency on posterior uncertainty and identify discretization strategies that avoid numerical artifacts. The framework is validated against exact posterior statistics, existing Bayesian PAT methods, and Hamiltonian Monte Carlo using the No-U-Turn Sampler (NUTS), and is demonstrated on a three-dimensional problem with approximately [MATH] unknowns on a general finite-element domain. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first large-scale Bayesian PAT study on general three-dimensional finite-element geometries, and the methodology extends naturally to a broad class of linear PDE-constrained inverse problems.
tldr: This paper develops a Bayesian uncertainty quantification framework for photoacoustic tomography, a biomedical imaging modality.
motivation: Photoacoustic tomography requires reliable uncertainty quantification for reconstructed images, but existing methods are computationally challenging for 3D problems and sensitive to numerical approximations.
method: The authors propose a matrix-free randomize-then-optimize (RTO) sampling strategy combined with finite-element discretization, ensuring adjoint consistency for efficient least-squares solvers.
result: The framework is validated against exact posterior statistics and Hamiltonian Monte Carlo, and demonstrated on a 3D problem with approximately 10^6 unknowns on a general finite-element domain.
conclusion: This is the first large-scale Bayesian PAT study on general 3D finite-element geometries, and the methodology extends to a broad class of linear PDE-constrained inverse problems.

title: Gpe: Evaluating Robust Evidence Aggregation For Fact Verification Under Controllable GEO-Style Poisoning
authors: Zhaoqi Wang, Zijian Zhang, Xiaomei Yuan, Pengtao Kou, Jiamou Liu, Zhen Li, Liehuang Zhu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.20730v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models increasingly use search tools to retrieve up-to-date information, introducing a new attack surface in which retrieved documents can be manipulated. This risk is amplified by the development of generative engine optimization, which can make selected content more likely to be retrieved, cited, and adopted by models. Existing fact-verification benchmarks and evaluation frameworks do not provide the controlled evidence environments needed to assess robustness against GEO poisoning. We therefore propose GPE, which consists of a multi-domain fact-verification benchmark and an evaluation framework for controlling evidence sources and poisoning ratios. Experiments across multiple verification methods and poisoning attacks demonstrate that GPE exposes robustness degradation and efficiency trade-offs that cannot be observed through clean evaluation alone, confirming the need to evaluate fact verification under adversarial evidence environments.
tldr: This paper proposes a benchmark and evaluation framework for assessing fact verification robustness against generative engine optimization poisoning.
motivation: Large language models using search tools are vulnerable to manipulated retrieved documents, but existing benchmarks lack controlled environments to evaluate robustness against such poisoning.
method: The authors introduce GPE, a multi-domain fact-verification benchmark with an evaluation framework that controls evidence sources and poisoning ratios, and test various verification methods under different poisoning attacks.
result: Experiments show that GPE reveals robustness degradation and efficiency trade-offs not observable in clean evaluation, confirming the need for adversarial evaluation.
conclusion: Fact verification systems must be evaluated under adversarial evidence environments to ensure reliability against GEO-style poisoning.

title: Explainable Belief Harmonization Under Dynamic Epistemic Partitions
authors: Jaros{\l}aw A. Chudziak Adam Kostka (warsaw University Of Technology)
abstract: ArXiv:2607.21210v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Existing approaches to multi-agent belief combination have established mature foundations for combining uncertain beliefs under common assumptions: consensus methods use iterative averaging, logic-based methods resolve conflicting knowledge bases, and epistemic logic analyzes agents' information states. Typically, these approaches assume that the structure determining what each agent can represent remains fixed. However, in many scenarios, agents gain or lose observational capacity during execution, and what was once admissible may become structurally impossible. This paper presents a formal framework for handling such runtime changes in epistemic partitions over continuous belief profiles. A hybrid approach exploits the advantages of answer set programming in elaboration tolerance, declarative integrity constraints, and explanations, with the numerical flexibility of Python. The framework applies to domains where agents operate at heterogeneous and possibly changing levels of resolution, and provides formal guarantees of admissibility preservation under refinement, unique mass-preserving repair under coarsening, and explanation completeness. Evaluation across 100 randomly generated topology changes confirms complete violation detection and explanation coverage.
tldr: A framework for belief harmonization under dynamic epistemic partitions using answer set programming and Python.
motivation: Existing belief combination methods assume fixed epistemic partitions, but agents may gain or lose observational capacity at runtime.
method: Hybrid approach combining answer set programming for declarative constraints and explanations with Python for numerical flexibility.
result: Formal guarantees of admissibility preservation under refinement, unique mass-preserving repair under coarsening, and explanation completeness; evaluated on 100 random topology changes.
conclusion: The framework effectively handles runtime changes in epistemic partitions, providing complete violation detection and explanation coverage.

title: Argon: A GNN-Empowered Compilation Framework For Scalable Neutral Atom Computing
authors: Wenjie Sun, Xiaoyu Li, Zhigang Wang, Lianhui Yu, Geng Chen, Guowu Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.21216v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Neutral atom quantum systems offer a promising pathway to large-scale quantum computing due to high qubit uniformity and flexible connectivity. To exploit this architecture, compilers must coordinate dynamic atom transport alongside highly parallel entangling gates. As circuits scale, the interplay between these operations becomes a system bottleneck, introducing denser logical interactions and longer temporal dependencies. Compilers must simultaneously satisfy rigid spatial constraints and complex movement schedules. Existing joint spatiotemporal compilation methods face an exponentially expanding search space, incurring substantial overheads or compromising fidelity as circuit size grows. In this work, we propose ARGON, a scalable compilation framework that introduces a spatiotemporal decoupling paradigm for neutral atom processors. Our key novelty is offloading static geometric conflict resolution to an offline phase, precomputing a library of hardware-certified, high-parallelism spatial layouts. To guide temporal routing, we deploy a Graph Neural Network (GNN) predictor to evaluate candidate layouts against deep temporal horizons, proactively evading downstream kinematic bottlenecks. Finally, a heuristic router translates the selected sequence into collision-free physical transport. Evaluations show ARGON completes compilation in under 10 seconds, delivering up to a >10^4x and 600x average speedup over state-of-the-art baselines. ARGON also minimizes routing decoherence and reduces Rydberg stages, improving execution fidelity by up to 10^2x on dense circuits.
tldr: A compilation framework for neutral atom quantum computers using GNN to optimize atom transport and gate scheduling.
motivation: Neutral atom quantum systems require efficient compilation to coordinate dynamic atom transport and parallel entangling gates, but existing methods face scalability issues.
method: Introduces a spatiotemporal decoupling paradigm with offline precomputation of spatial layouts and a GNN predictor to evaluate candidate layouts for temporal routing.
result: Completes compilation in under 10 seconds, achieving up to 10^4x speedup and 10^2x fidelity improvement over baselines.
conclusion: The framework significantly improves compilation efficiency and execution fidelity for large-scale neutral atom circuits.

title: Is MoE Routing A Huffman Code? Discovering The Frequency-Diversity Law In Chain-of-Thought
authors: Ching-Chieh Tsao, Zhuoyi Lin, Wenya Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.20427v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Mixture-of-Experts architectures have revolutionized scaling, yet the underlying logic of their routing remains a black box. In this paper, we uncover a fundamental governing principle: MoE routing is not merely selection, but a manifestation of Huffman Coding. We introduce the Frequency-Diversity Law, revealing that state-of-the-art models, such as Phi-3.5-MoE and Gemma-4-27B-A4B, spontaneously act as information-theoretic engines. These models allocate sparse expert resources for common tokens while invoking high-diversity expert committees for rare, complex tasks found in chain-of-thought trajectories. However, we identify a critical redundancy trap in Qwen3.5-35B-A3B: when effective sparsity (k/E_eff) is sufficiently low, load-balancing inadvertently imposes functional redundancy, masking the underlying Huffman efficiency signal. To bridge this gap, we propose Subset Difference Pruning, a surgical strategy to eliminate functional duplicates. We demonstrate that pruning does not degrade reasoning; instead, it unleashes the model's latent Huffman efficiency, forcing the logic to collapse into streamlined, high-density paths. Our findings suggest that the next generation of MoEs should move beyond forced load-balancing toward Minimum Description Length (MDL) optimality, assigning shorter expert-routing codes to high-frequency information and longer, more diverse codes to low-frequency information, thereby transforming routing from a heuristic into a principled compression engine.
tldr: This paper interprets MoE routing as a Huffman coding mechanism and proposes a pruning strategy to improve efficiency.
motivation: The authors aim to demystify the black-box routing in Mixture-of-Experts models by uncovering a fundamental principle analogous to Huffman coding.
method: They introduce the Frequency-Diversity Law, analyze routing patterns in state-of-the-art MoE models, and propose Subset Difference Pruning to eliminate functional redundancy.
result: They find that MoE models naturally allocate sparse resources to common tokens and diverse committees to rare tokens, but load-balancing can mask this efficiency; pruning restores it without degrading reasoning.
conclusion: Future MoE designs should move toward Minimum Description Length optimality, treating routing as a compression engine rather than a heuristic.

result: Long-lived phonon waves and orientation-dependent heat transport were observed at room temperature, confirming phonon focusing.

Author(s): Tongrui Li, Yuzhe Wang, Haoyuan Yan, Jiexiong Sun, Rui Xu, Jianghao Yao, Sen Liao, Shiwu Su, Yunbo Wu, Zhanfeng Liu, Yilin Wang, Zhe Sun, Donglai Feng, and Juan Jiang

Electron-plasmon coupling, in which carriers are dressed by collective electronic oscillations, represents an important many-body interaction in solids. Here, using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy, we report the tunable electron-plasmon coupling in the layered transition metal dichalcogeni…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045121] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports tunable electron-plasmon coupling in a layered transition metal dichalcogenide using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy.
motivation: To study electron-plasmon coupling, an important many-body interaction in solids, and demonstrate its tunability in a specific material system.
method: Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) was used to measure the electronic structure and plasmonic effects in ZrSe2-xTex alloys.
result: The electron-plasmon coupling strength can be tuned by varying the tellurium concentration in the alloy.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into many-body interactions in layered materials and may have implications for plasmonics and optoelectronics.

title: Large Earthquakes Follow Highly Unequal Ones
authors: Sudip Sarkar And Soumyajyoti Biswas
abstract:
Author(s): Sudip Sarkar and Soumyajyoti Biswas

It was conjectured for a long time that the tectonic plates are in a self-organized state of criticality and that the Gutenberg-Richter law is a manifestation of that. It was recently shown that for a system near criticality, the inequality of their responses due to external driving would sharply ri…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014143] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies inequality of earthquake magnitudes as a signature of criticality in tectonic plates, using a fiber bundle model.
motivation: To test the conjecture that tectonic plates are in a self-organized critical state and that the Gutenberg-Richter law is a manifestation of it.
method: Analyzes inequality measures (e.g., Gini index) of earthquake magnitudes from a fiber bundle model and real earthquake catalogs.
result: Large earthquakes tend to follow periods of high inequality in earthquake magnitudes, suggesting a precursory signal.
conclusion: Inequality of earthquake magnitudes can serve as a potential precursor for large earthquakes, supporting the criticality hypothesis.

title: Multiscale Feedback Drives Viral Evolution And Epidemic Dynamics
authors: Juan C. Muñoz-Sánchez, J. Tomás Lázaro, Josep Sardanyés, And Santiago F. Elena
abstract:
Author(s): Juan C. Muñoz-Sánchez, J. Tomás Lázaro, Josep Sardanyés, and Santiago F. Elena

We introduce a minimal multiscale framework that links within-host virus dynamics to population-level susceptible-infectious-recovered-susceptible (SIRS) epidemiology through explicit, bidirectional coupling. At the microscopic layer, a two-variant quasispecies (master and mutant genomes with packag…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033097] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: A multiscale model coupling within-host viral quasispecies dynamics to population-level SIRS epidemiology.
motivation: To understand how within-host viral evolution and feedback with epidemic dynamics shape viral emergence and disease spread.
method: Develops a minimal mathematical framework with bidirectional coupling between a two-variant quasispecies model and a SIRS compartmental model.
result: The model shows that multiscale feedback can lead to complex epidemic patterns including oscillations and extinction.
conclusion: Multiscale feedback is crucial for realistic modeling of viral evolution and epidemic dynamics.

title: Exactly Solvable Population Model With Square-root Growth Noise And Cell-size Regulation
authors: Farshid Jafarpour
abstract:
Author(s): Farshid Jafarpour

Stochastic exponential growth is nearly ubiquitous across cellular life, but how its microscopic noise structure shapes population growth remains poorly understood. Here, we introduce an exactly solvable population model in which cells grow exponentially with fluctuations that scale with the square …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033082] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an exactly solvable stochastic population model with square-root growth noise and cell-size regulation.
motivation: Understanding how microscopic noise structure affects population growth in cellular systems is poorly understood.
method: The author introduces a stochastic model where cells grow exponentially with fluctuations scaling as the square root of cell size, and solves it exactly.
result: The model yields exact analytical expressions for population dynamics and size distributions.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for stochastic exponential growth with cell-size regulation, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Mie-tronics Supermodes And Symmetry Breaking In Nonlocal Metasurfaces
authors: Thanh Xuan Hoang, Ayan Nussupbekov, Jie Ji, Daniel Leykam, Jaime Gómez Rivas, And Yuri Kivshar
abstract:
Author(s): Thanh Xuan Hoang, Ayan Nussupbekov, Jie Ji, Daniel Leykam, Jaime Gómez Rivas, and Yuri Kivshar

It is usually believed that symmetry breaking in photonic systems leads to weaker confinement, such as in the case of metasurfaces when bound states in the continuum are replaced by quasibound states with lower quality [MATH] factors.
